The element must already be focused or in edit mode (use double_click_at or click_at first). Related: type_text (for real DOM input fields), double_click_at (enter edit mode in canvas editors before inserting text), click_at (focus canvas element before inserting). Multi-agent: agent-scoped tabs; cross-agent reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED; cap configurable (default 8, 1-64). Pass tab_id only when this agent owns multiple tabs; auto-resolves otherwise. RETURNS change_report: when this tool runs, the response includes a `change_report` field with a compact diff of what the action mutated (URL, dialogs_opened, nodes_added, nodes_removed, attrs_changed, inputs_changed, focus_shift). Use this to learn the consequence without calling read_page next. If the report exceeds the size cap, `change_report.truncated:true` and `change_report_hint` are set; call read_page for the full state.

name: double_click_at
description: Double-click at specific viewport coordinates using CDP trusted events. Dispatches two rapid mousePressed/mouseReleased cycles with clickCount=2 on the second pair. Supports modifier keys. Coordinates are CSS pixels relative to the browser viewport. When to use: for entering edit mode in canvas-based editors (Excalidraw text boxes, Google Sheets cells), selecting words in contenteditable elements, or any double-click on coordinate-targeted elements. Related: click_at (single click at coordinates), double_click (double-click DOM elements by selector), insert_text (type text after entering edit mode via double-click). Multi-agent: agent-scoped tabs; cross-agent reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED; cap configurable (default 8, 1-64). Pass tab_id only when this agent owns multiple tabs; auto-resolves otherwise. RETURNS change_report: when this tool runs, the response includes a `change_report` field with a compact diff of what the action mutated (URL, dialogs_opened, nodes_added, nodes_removed, attrs_changed, inputs_changed, focus_shift). Use this to learn the consequence without calling read_page next. If the report exceeds the size cap, `change_report.truncated:true` and `change_report_hint` are set; call read_page for the full state.

name: set_attribute
description: Set an HTML attribute value on an element. Returns confirmation. When to use: to modify element attributes for form manipulation, changing hidden field values, toggling ARIA states, or setting data attributes. Related: get_attribute (read attribute value first), get_dom_snapshot (find element selectors). Multi-agent: agent-scoped tabs; cross-agent reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED; cap configurable (default 8, 1-64). Pass tab_id only when this agent owns multiple tabs; auto-resolves otherwise. RETURNS change_report: when this tool runs, the response includes a `change_report` field with a compact diff of what the action mutated (URL, dialogs_opened, nodes_added, nodes_removed, attrs_changed, inputs_changed, focus_shift). Use this to learn the consequence without calling read_page next. If the report exceeds the size cap, `change_report.truncated:true` and `change_report_hint` are set; call read_page for the full state.

name: read_sheet
description: Read cell values from a spreadsheet range. Returns cell values as array. When to use: to extract tabular data from a spreadsheet. Related: fill_sheet (write data), navigate (go to the spreadsheet first). Multi-agent: agent-scoped tabs; cross-agent reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED; cap configurable (default 8, 1-64). Pass tab_id only when this agent owns multiple tabs; auto-resolves otherwise.

name: read_page
description: Read the text content of the current page. When to use: as the FIRST step after navigating to understand what is on the page. Automatically waits for DOM stability on JS-heavy sites. Returns main content prioritized over sidebars/nav/footer, capped at ~8K chars. Related: get_dom_snapshot (get structured element data with selectors for interaction), navigate (go to a page first), scroll (scroll to load more content before reading). Multi-agent: agent-scoped tabs; cross-agent reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED; cap configurable (default 8, 1-64). Pass tab_id only when this agent owns multiple tabs; auto-resolves otherwise.

name: get_text
description: Get the text content of a specific element. Returns the element's text. When to use: to read a specific element's text without reading the whole page. Related: read_page (read full page), get_attribute (read element attributes like href, src). Multi-agent: agent-scoped tabs; cross-agent reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED; cap configurable (default 8, 1-64). Pass tab_id only when this agent owns multiple tabs; auto-resolves otherwise.

name: get_attribute
description: Get an HTML attribute value from an element. Returns the attribute value. When to use: to read href, src, value, data attributes, or ARIA properties from an element. Related: get_text (read element text content), get_dom_snapshot (find element selectors). Multi-agent: agent-scoped tabs; cross-agent reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED; cap configurable (default 8, 1-64). Pass tab_id only when this agent owns multiple tabs; auto-resolves otherwise.

name: get_dom_snapshot
description: Get a structured DOM snapshot with element references (e.g., e1, e2, e3). When to use: BEFORE any interaction tool (click, type_text, etc.) to find the right selector or element ref. Returns elements with tag, text, attributes, and position data. Element refs like 'e5' can be passed directly to click, type_text, hover, and other tools. Related: read_page (quick text content), click/type_text/hover (use refs from this snapshot). Multi-agent: agent-scoped tabs; cross-agent reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED; cap configurable (default 8, 1-64). Pass tab_id only when this agent owns multiple tabs; auto-resolves otherwise.

name: list_tabs
description: List all open browser tabs with title, URL, and active status. Returns array of tab objects. When to use: to see all open tabs before switching. Related: switch_tab (switch to a tab by ID), open_tab (open a new tab). Multi-agent: agent-scoped tabs; cross-agent reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED; cap configurable (default 8, 1-64).

name: get_page_snapshot
description: Get a markdown snapshot of the current page DOM. Returns interactive elements with ref IDs for targeting. When to use: BEFORE any click/type/interaction to see current page state. Call this at the start of each new page or when you need to find elements. Related: read_page (plain text content), get_text (single element text). Multi-agent: agent-scoped tabs; cross-agent reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED; cap configurable (default 8, 1-64). Pass tab_id only when this agent owns multiple tabs; auto-resolves otherwise.

name: get_site_guide
description: Get site-specific automation guidance for a domain. Returns selectors, navigation patterns, and tips for automating the site. When to use: when starting work on a new site or when standard selectors fail. Related: get_page_snapshot (see current elements), get_dom_snapshot (raw DOM). Multi-agent: agent-scoped tabs; cross-agent reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED; cap configurable (default 8, 1-64).

name: list_sessions
description: List all past FSB automation sessions with summary info (task, status, duration, action count, cost). Use to find session IDs for deeper inspection with get_session_detail. Related: get_session_detail (inspect a specific session), get_logs (get raw logs).

name: get_session_detail
description: Get full detail for an automation session including logs, action history, and timing. Use after list_sessions to inspect what happened. For an in-flight session id (one that get_task_status reports as currentSessionId), returns a partial snapshot with `final: false` and the latest known action; the full payload becomes available once the session finishes. Returns structured JSON or human-readable text report. Related: list_sessions (find session IDs first), get_logs (get raw log entries), get_task_status (check if a session is still in flight).

name: get_logs
description: Get recent automation logs or logs for a specific session. Includes error/warning summary report. Use to debug issues or understand what FSB has been doing.

name: search_memory
description: Search FSB's memory system for relevant past experiences. Returns memories ranked by relevance with keyword matching and recency scoring. Use to find what FSB learned from previous tasks on similar sites or domains. When to use: before automating a site to check if FSB has learned relevant patterns from past sessions. Related: get_memory_stats (check memory size), list_sessions (find specific sessions).

name: get_memory_stats
description: Get FSB memory system statistics including total count, type breakdown, and storage usage. Use to understand how much FSB has learned from past sessions.

name: back
description: Navigate one step back in browser history on the agent's active tab. Single-step only (no back(n)); no companion forward tool in v0.9.60. Agent-scoped: targets the agent's active tab unless tab_id is supplied. Ownership-enforced via the Phase 240 dispatch gate -- cross-agent calls reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED. Returns a structured result of shape { status, resultingUrl, historyDepth } where status is one of: ok (back navigation settled cleanly), no_history (history depth <= 1, nothing to go back to), cross_origin (target page is on a different origin from the source), bf_cache (back was served from the back/forward cache and the pageshow listener observed event.persisted=true), fragment_only (only the URL fragment changed via history navigation). Background-tab compatible: does not steal focus or call chrome.tabs.update({active: true}). Multi-agent contract: agent_id is FSB-issued and required (the server captures it via agent:register on first tool call -- callers do not provide it). tab_id is agent-scoped: only tabs owned by the calling agent can be addressed. The concurrency cap is configurable (default 8, range 1-64); the (N+1)th agent claim is rejected with AGENT_CAP_REACHED { cap, active }. Ownership enforcement: cross-agent calls reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED; incognito tabs reject with TAB_INCOGNITO_NOT_SUPPORTED; cross-window tabs reject with TAB_OUT_OF_SCOPE. Tool-specific typed error codes returnable by this tool: NO_BACK_HISTORY, CROSS_ORIGIN, BF_CACHE, FRAGMENT_ONLY. RETURNS change_report: the response includes a `change_report` field with a compact diff of what the back navigation mutated (URL, dialogs_opened, nodes_added, nodes_removed, attrs_changed, inputs_changed, focus_shift). Cross-origin transitions emit a URL-only report with `cross_origin:true`. Use this to learn the consequence without calling read_page next; if `change_report.truncated:true` is set, call read_page for the full state.

name: list_credentials
description: List saved credentials. Returns domain and username pairs only -- passwords are never included in the response. Use fill_credential to autofill a login form.

name: fill_credential
description: Auto-fill login form on the active tab with a saved credential. The password is resolved inside the extension and injected directly into the page -- it never crosses the WebSocket bridge. The domain parameter is accepted for backward compatibility but the actual lookup domain is derived from the tab URL for security. Requires the credential vault to be unlocked. Multi-agent: agent-scoped tabs; cross-agent reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED. Pass tab_id only when this agent owns multiple tabs; auto-resolves otherwise.

name: list_payment_methods
description: List saved payment methods. Returns card brand, last 4 digits, and cardholder name only -- full card numbers and CVV are never included. Use use_payment_method to fill a checkout form.

name: use_payment_method
description: Fill checkout form on the active tab with a saved payment method. Shows a confirmation prompt with card brand, last 4 digits, and merchant domain before any fill occurs. The fill domain is derived from the resolved tab URL inside the extension, not from this request. Requires both credential vault and payment access to be unlocked. Multi-agent: agent-scoped tabs; cross-agent reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED. Pass tab_id only when this agent owns multiple tabs; auto-resolves otherwise.

name: run_task
description: IMPORTANT: Only use this tool if the user explicitly requests autopilot, asks to "run a task", or says "let FSB handle it". For all other browser tasks, use the manual tools (navigate, read_page, get_dom_snapshot, click, type_text, execute_js, etc.) to accomplish the task step by step -- they are more reliable and give you full control. This tool hands control to FSB's built-in AI which decides the steps autonomously. Returns a completion summary with success status and action log. Multi-agent contract: agent_id is FSB-issued and required (the server captures it via agent:register on first tool call -- callers do not provide it). The concurrency cap is configurable (default 8, range 1-64); the (N+1)th agent claim is rejected with AGENT_CAP_REACHED { cap, active }. Ownership enforcement: cross-agent calls reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED; incognito tabs reject with TAB_INCOGNITO_NOT_SUPPORTED; cross-window tabs reject with TAB_OUT_OF_SCOPE.

name: stop_task
description: Cancel the currently running automation task. Returns confirmation of cancellation. When to use: when run_task is taking too long, heading in the wrong direction, or you need to regain manual control. Related: get_task_status (check progress before deciding to stop), run_task (the task being cancelled). Agent-scoped: only the calling agent's task is cancelled; cross-agent calls reject with TAB_NOT_OWNED.

name: get_task_status
description: Check whether a task is currently running and its progress. Use to poll status when not receiving progress notifications. Returns percent complete, current phase, and ETA. Related: run_task (the task being monitored), stop_task (cancel if needed). Agent-scoped: returns the calling agent's task status only.

name: generate_ppt_by_topic
description: Generate PowerPoint presentations from topics

name: forgecraft
description: Setup-time tool for engineering standards. Diagnoses project state. Remove this MCP server after setup is complete to save tokens.

name: forgecraft_actions
description: Full ForgeCraft action suite. Use action='setup_project' to onboard, 'check_cascade' to verify GS steps, 'generate_session_prompt' for a bound prompt, 'audit' for compliance score. Remove after setup to save tokens.

name: get_godot_status
description: Check if Godot editor is connected to the MCP server.

name: get_guide
description: Read a short markdown guide from the server. Same content as the MCP resources/read protocol, exposed as a tool so it works in MCP clients that do not support resources (e.g. Claude Desktop, Cursor chat). Call with no args to list available guides: testing-loop, scene-editing, asset-generation, troubleshooting, tool-index. Call with {slug: "..."} to get the full markdown. Useful when a workflow is non-obvious (testing a running game, choosing between scene-editing tools, troubleshooting "Runtime helper not connected", etc.).

name: list_dir
description: List files and folders under a Godot project path (e.g., res://). Returns arrays of files and folders in the specified directory.

name: read_file
description: Read a text file from the Godot project, optionally a specific line range. Useful for reading GDScript files, scene files, or any text-based content.

name: search_project
description: Search the Godot project for a substring and return file hits with line numbers. Useful for finding usages of functions, variables, or any text pattern.

name: create_script
description: Create a NEW GDScript file (.gd) that does not exist yet. Use this for creating new scripts, NOT for editing existing files (use edit_script for edits). Use classdb_query to verify unfamiliar Godot class methods. After creating a script, consider using run_scene to test and get_errors to check for issues.

name: create_scene
description: Create a new Godot scene (.tscn) file with nodes. Use this to create player scenes, UI screens, game objects, etc.

name: read_scene
description: Read and parse a scene file to get its full node structure and properties. Use this to understand a scene before editing.

name: add_node
description: Add a node to an existing scene file. Supports an optional script attachment, group memberships, and a tree of children created in the same call (1 tool call instead of N). Children format: {name|node_name, type|node_type, properties?, script?, groups?, children?}. Both key styles are accepted so children can reuse the same keys you use at the top level (node_name, node_type) or the shorter form (name, type). Unknown child keys are rejected with a clear error.

name: remove_node
description: Remove a node from an existing scene file.

name: modify_node_property
description: Modify a single property on a node in a .tscn scene file. For multiple properties at once use set_node_properties. ALWAYS use a tool to modify .tscn files — NEVER edit them as text. To attach or change a script, use attach_script (NOT modify_node_property with property="script") — modify_node_property only rewrites the .tscn on disk, leaving the editor's in-memory node without the script, which makes connect_signal fail.

name: rename_node
description: Rename a node in a scene.

name: move_node
description: Move a node to a different parent in a scene and optionally control its position among siblings.

name: attach_script
description: Attach or change a script on a node in a scene.

name: detach_script
description: Remove a script from a node in a scene.

name: set_collision_shape
description: Create and assign a collision shape resource to a CollisionShape2D or CollisionShape3D node. Supports: CircleShape2D, RectangleShape2D, CapsuleShape2D, SphereShape3D, BoxShape3D, etc.

name: set_sprite_texture
description:
Assign a texture resource to a Sprite2D / Sprite3D / TextureRect node in a .tscn scene file. Modes:
  • FromPath  — load any texture file from disk (png/jpg/webp/svg/.tres) via load(). Returns whatever Texture2D the importer produced (usually CompressedTexture2D). Most common after generate_2d_asset.
  • ImageTexture (DEPRECATED ALIAS for FromPath, kept for back-compat)
  • NewImageTexture — force-create an ImageTexture (in-memory) from a raw image file.
  • PlaceholderTexture2D — in-scene placeholder of a given size.
  • GradientTexture2D / NoiseTexture2D — procedural textures.
Response always includes texture_class (the actual Godot class the texture decoded to), width, height, and texture_path so the agent can confirm what landed without an extra get_resource_info call.

name: instance_scene
description: Add an instance of another scene (.tscn) as a child node. This is how you compose scenes from reusable parts (like prefabs). The instance maintains a live reference to the source scene. Use this instead of add_node when you want to reuse an existing scene.

name: set_mesh
description: Create and assign a mesh resource to a MeshInstance3D node. REQUIRED to make 3D geometry visible. Primitive types: BoxMesh, SphereMesh, CylinderMesh, CapsuleMesh, PlaneMesh, PrismMesh, TorusMesh, QuadMesh, TextMesh. Or load from file.

name: set_material
description: Create and assign a material to a MeshInstance3D, CSG, or GeometryInstance3D node. Supports StandardMaterial3D or loading from file.

name: get_node_spatial_info
description: Query computed 3D spatial data for a Node3D in a scene file. Returns local/global positions, scales, rotation quaternions, and subtree bounding boxes (AABB) when available. Use this before making precise 3D placement decisions.

name: measure_node_distance
description: Measure the world-space distance between two Node3D nodes in a scene file. Returns both the full 3D delta and the horizontal XZ distance.

name: snap_node_to_grid
description: Snap a Node3D position to a grid in local or global space. Useful for modular level building and keeping 3D scenes aligned.

name: set_node_properties
description: Set MULTIPLE properties on a node in a single tool call. Non-atomic: each property is applied independently; the response separates "applied" from "failed" so partial success surfaces clearly. Saves the scene once at the end. Resource-typed properties must use set_resource_property / set_sprite_texture / etc.

name: set_node_groups
description: Set, add, or remove a node's group memberships in a .tscn scene file. Groups persist to disk so the running game can call get_tree().get_nodes_in_group(name).

name: get_node_groups
description: Read the list of groups a node belongs to in a .tscn scene file.

name: find_nodes_in_group
description: Find every node in a .tscn that belongs to a given group. Returns paths, names, and types. Useful for verifying that level.gd will actually pick up the right nodes via get_tree().get_nodes_in_group().

name: set_resource_property
description: Modify a property on a Resource that is currently held by a node (or by another resource attached to that node). Use this to tweak shape radii, material colors, gradient stops, etc., WITHOUT recreating the resource. resource_path walks from the node down to the resource using "/"-separated property names, e.g. "shape", "material", or "material/next_pass". After the change, saves the scene.

name: save_resource_to_file
description: Save a Resource currently held by a node (or sub-resource) to a standalone .tres file so it can be referenced by other scenes / shared / committed. The node's property is then re-pointed to the loaded-from-disk version, so future set_resource_property calls write through to that file. Works for any Resource subclass: Material, Mesh, Shape, Curve, Gradient, etc.

name: get_resource_info
description:
Inspect ANY Godot Resource. Two modes:
  • path mode: pass {path: "res://foo.png"} for a resource on disk (.tres / .res / image / .glb / .ogg / .tscn / etc.)
  • node mode: pass {scene_path, node_path, resource_property} to inspect a resource attached to a node WITHOUT having to save it as .tres first (e.g. the shape on a CollisionShape2D, the material on a MeshInstance3D, the stream on an AudioStreamPlayer).
Returns class, file size (path mode), and type-specific info: width/height for textures, vertex/surface counts and AABB for meshes, length for AudioStream/Animation, node count for PackedScene, common Material properties, Shape extents, and the resource's dependencies.

name: list_signal_connections
description: List signal connections involving a node. source="scene_file" (default) reads connections persisted to a .tscn. source="runtime" requires the game to be running and reads live connections from the SceneTree. Use the runtime mode to verify dynamically-connected signals (those connected from code in _ready, not in the editor).

name: connect_signal
description: Connect a signal between two nodes inside a .tscn scene file. The target script must define the method (will refuse otherwise). Equivalent to clicking the "+" in the editor's Node > Signals panel and persists the connection to the .tscn. NOTE: scripts must be attached via attach_script (NOT via modify_node_property), otherwise the editor's in-memory node will not see the script and this tool will reject the connection.

name: disconnect_signal
description: Remove a signal connection from a .tscn scene file. No-op if the connection doesn't exist.

name: edit_script
description: Apply a SMALL, SURGICAL code edit (1-10 lines) to GDScript files. Auto-applies changes. For large changes, call multiple times. ONLY for .gd files - NEVER for .tscn scene files. Use classdb_query to verify unfamiliar Godot class methods. After making changes, consider using run_scene to test and get_errors to check for issues.

name: validate_script
description: Validate a GDScript file for syntax errors using Godot's built-in parser. Call after creating or modifying scripts to ensure they are error-free.

name: create_folder
description: Create a directory (with parent directories if needed).

name: delete_file
description: Permanently delete a file from the project. REQUIRES confirm=true as an explicit safety gate — omitting confirm returns an error. Creates a .bak backup alongside the original by default (disable with create_backup=false). REFUSES if the file is currently open in the editor (any scene tab or script editor tab); close the tab first, or pass force=true to bypass the check (not recommended — deleting the active scene out from under the editor can crash Godot). Use ONLY when deletion is explicitly requested; NEVER as a way to "edit" or "reset" a file (use edit_script instead). Does not delete directories.

name: rename_file
description: Rename or move a file, optionally updating references in other files.

name: list_scripts
description: List all GDScript files in the project with basic metadata.

name: get_project_settings
description: Concise project settings summary: main_scene, window size/stretch, physics tick rate, and render basics.

name: get_input_map
description: Return the full InputMap: built-in actions (ui_*, spatial_editor/*) plus all project-defined actions from project.godot. Each action maps to an object with "events" (array of key/mouse/gamepad bindings) and optionally "deadzone". Use this before configure_input_map to see current bindings and deadzones.

name: get_collision_layers
description: Return named 2D/3D physics collision layers from ProjectSettings.

name: get_node_properties
description: Get available properties for a Godot node type. Use this to discover what properties exist on a node type (e.g., anchors_preset for Control, position for Node2D).

name: get_console_log
description: Return the latest lines from the Godot editor output log.

name: get_errors
description: Get errors and warnings from both the Godot Output panel and the Debugger > Errors tab. Returns file paths, line numbers, severity, stack traces, and which source each error came from. If errors mention a missing method or property, use classdb_query to verify the correct API before fixing.

name: clear_console_log
description: Mark the current position in the Godot editor log. Subsequent get_console_log and get_errors calls will only return output after this point.

name: open_in_godot
description: Open a file in the Godot editor at a specific line (side-effect only).

name: scene_tree_dump
description: Dump the scene tree of the scene currently open in the Godot editor (node names, types, and attached scripts).

name: list_settings
description: Browse Godot project settings by category. Returns values from the editor's in-memory state — this matches project.godot after a normal Godot save, but direct edits to project.godot on disk are not reflected until the editor restarts (rescan_filesystem does not help). Call without a category to see all available categories. Call with a category to see all settings with their current values, types, and valid options.

name: update_project_settings
description: Update one or more Godot project settings. Pass a dictionary of setting paths to their new values. Use list_settings first to discover available setting paths, current values, and valid options for a category. For input action bindings, prefer configure_input_map — if you do pass input/* keys here, partial updates are merged safely (existing events are preserved).

name: configure_input_map
description: Add, remove, or replace input actions and their key/button bindings. Use get_input_map to see current actions before modifying.

name: run_scene
description: Launch a scene in the Godot editor. By default the call BLOCKS until the editor flips to playing state (so the next get_errors / take_screenshot / send_input call sees a real game). The response includes started, runtime_connected, wait_for_started_ms, wait_for_runtime_ms, scene_path, and runtime_root. Use runtime_root (e.g. "/root/Main") as the prefix for query_runtime_node node_path arguments — it is computed from the actual root node name in the .tscn, NOT from the file name. Set wait_for_runtime=true to additionally wait for the in-game MCPRuntime helper to connect (required before take_screenshot / send_input will work). Recommended testing loop: run_scene({wait_for_runtime:true}) → query_runtime_node / send_input / take_screenshot → get_errors → stop_scene.

name: stop_scene
description: Stop the currently running scene in the Godot editor. Always stop the scene before editing code to avoid errors repeating every frame.

name: is_playing
description: Compatibility shim: returns {playing, scene}. For richer info (uptime, runtime helper connectivity, last-launched target) prefer get_runtime_status.

name: get_runtime_status
description: Combined editor + runtime status snapshot. Returns playing, playing_scene, last_launched ("current"|"main"|res-path), uptime_ms since the most recent run_scene, and runtime_helper_connected (true once the in-game MCPRuntime autoload is talking to the MCP server).

name: wait
description: Sleep server-side. Useful between input events to let the game process them. Capped at 30000ms / 30s. Pass either ms or seconds (ms wins if both given).

name: take_screenshot
description: Capture the current viewport of the running game and save it as a PNG. REQUIRES the game to be running with the MCPRuntime autoload connected (run_scene with wait_for_runtime=true first). Returns resource_path, absolute_path, width, height, and (optionally) base64_png. Default save location is res://addons/godot_mcp/cache/screenshots/.

name: send_input
description: Synthesize an InputEvent and dispatch it to the running game via Input.parse_input_event. REQUIRES the game to be running with the MCPRuntime autoload connected. Use this to drive automated tests: click buttons, press keys, fire input actions. For multi-step interactions, alternate send_input → wait → query_runtime_node / take_screenshot.

name: query_runtime_node
description: Query a live node in the running scene tree. REQUIRES the game to be running with the MCPRuntime autoload connected. Returns class, path, valid, groups, and a map of property values. By default returns position, global_position, rotation, scale, visible, modulate — pass `properties:["..."]` to override. Set include_children=true to also list direct child nodes.

name: get_runtime_log
description: Return entries from the MCPRuntime in-game ring buffer. The buffer holds the last ~500 lines pushed via MCPRuntime.push_runtime_log(level, text) from your scripts plus internal connection events. For full engine stdout (script prints, errors, warnings) use get_console_log — the editor already captures the running game's stdout. Returns entries with ts_ms, level, and text plus started_at_ms (when the helper started) and now_ms.

name: classdb_query
description: Query Godot's ClassDB for class information: properties, methods, signals, and inheritance. Use this to verify that a class, method, or property actually exists in the running Godot engine before writing code. Prevents using wrong method names, outdated Godot 3 API, or incorrect signatures.

name: rescan_filesystem
description: Trigger a full filesystem rescan in the Godot editor. Use after creating, deleting, or modifying files externally (e.g. from the terminal or another tool). The scan is asynchronous and returns immediately.

name: setup_autoload
description: Register, unregister, or list autoload singletons. Autoloads are scripts/scenes loaded automatically at project start.

name: generate_2d_asset

name: check_code
description: Analyze inline code for security vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10, XSS, SQL injection, insecure patterns). Pass code as a string parameter. For scanning files on disk, use scan_file instead. Example: check_code({code: 'app.get(...)', language: 'javascript'})

name: check_project
description: Scan multiple files for security vulnerabilities and generate a project-wide security report with a security score. Use this for comprehensive security audits.

name: get_security_docs
description: Get security best practices and remediation guidance for a specific topic, framework, or vulnerability type. Covers OWASP Top 10, framework-specific hardening (Next.js, Supabase, Stripe), and secure coding patterns. Returns actionable guidance with code examples.

name: check_dependencies
description: Check npm, PyPI, or Go packages for known security vulnerabilities (CVEs) using the OSV database. Use this before adding new dependencies or to audit existing ones.

name: scan_directory
description: Scan all files in a directory on disk for security vulnerabilities. Pass a directory path — reads files from filesystem. Returns security score (A-F) and findings. Results may be truncated for large projects — check fileRanking in JSON output for top files. Example: scan_directory({path: './src'})

name: scan_dependencies
description: Parse a lockfile or manifest (package.json, package-lock.json, requirements.txt, go.mod) and check all dependencies for known CVEs via the OSV database. Reads the file directly. Use this after installing dependencies, during CI, or when auditing existing projects for vulnerable packages.

name: scan_secrets
description: Scan files and directories for leaked secrets, API keys, tokens, and credentials. Detects high-entropy strings, known API key patterns (AWS, Stripe, OpenAI, GitHub, Supabase), exposed .env files, and missing .gitignore coverage. Returns findings with exact line numbers and remediation steps.

name: scan_staged
description: Scan git-staged files for security vulnerabilities before committing. Run this before every commit to catch issues early. No input needed — automatically reads staged files.

name: compliance_report
description: Map security findings to compliance controls (SOC2, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, ISO27001, EUAIACT). Scans a directory and groups issues by control. Output includes a summary section at the top; for large projects, findings are truncated to top 50. Use mode=executive for C-level summary. Example: compliance_report({path: '.', framework: 'SOC2'})

name: export_sarif
description: Scan a directory and export results in SARIF v2.1.0 format for CI/CD integration (GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps). Returns JSON string.

name: check_package_health
description: Check npm packages for typosquat risk, maintenance status, adoption metrics, and deprecation. Use this before adding new dependencies to catch suspicious or risky packages.

name: fix_code
description: Pass vulnerable code as a string and get fix suggestions with before/after patches. Returns structured edit instructions (line numbers, severity, confidence). Use verify_fix afterwards to confirm the fix resolved the issue. Example: fix_code({code: '...', language: 'typescript'})

name: audit_config
description: Audit application config files (next.config, middleware, .env, vercel.json) for cross-file security gaps: missing headers, unprotected routes, exposed secrets. NOT the same as guardvibe_doctor which checks AI host security (MCP configs, hooks). Example: audit_config({path: '.'})

name: generate_policy
description: Auto-detect project stack (Next.js, Supabase, Stripe, Clerk, Prisma, etc.) and generate tailored security policies. Outputs ready-to-use CSP headers, CORS configuration, Supabase RLS policies, rate limiting rules, and security headers based on detected frameworks.

name: review_pr
description: Review a pull request for security issues. Scans only changed lines (diff-only mode) and produces output for GitHub Check Runs, PR comments, or inline annotations. Supports severity gating to block PRs.

name: scan_secrets_history
description: Scan git history for leaked secrets. Finds secrets that were committed in the past — even if they were later removed. Marks each finding as 'active' (still in code) or 'removed' (in git history only, needs rotation).

name: policy_check
description: Check project against compliance policies defined in .guardviberc. Use this in CI/CD pipelines to enforce security gates, or before releases to verify compliance requirements are met. Validates custom framework requirements, severity thresholds, required controls, and risk exceptions. Returns pass/fail status with detailed findings per control.

name: analyze_dataflow
description: Track user input (request body, URL params, form data) flowing into dangerous sinks (SQL queries, eval, file operations, redirects). Detects injection vulnerabilities that regex rules miss by following variable assignments through code.

name: analyze_cross_file_dataflow
description: Track user input flowing across module boundaries — detects injection vulnerabilities spanning multiple files. Pass files array with file contents. For single-file analysis, use analyze_dataflow instead. Example: analyze_cross_file_dataflow({files: [{path: 'src/api.ts', content: '...'}, {path: 'src/db.ts', content: '...'}]})

name: check_command
description: Analyze a shell command for security risks before execution. Returns allow/ask/deny verdict with blast radius, safer alternatives, and context-aware risk assessment. Detects: destructive ops, git history rewrites, secret exposure, data exfiltration, deploy triggers, privilege escalation, database drops.

name: scan_config_change
description: Compare before/after versions of a config file to detect security downgrades: CORS relaxation, CSP weakening, HSTS removal, debug mode, cookie flag changes, TLS disabling, new hardcoded secrets, removed security headers.

name: repo_security_posture
description: Analyze a repository's overall security posture. Maps sensitive areas (auth, payments, PII, admin, API, infrastructure), identifies high-risk workflows, recommends guard mode, and lists priority fixes.

name: explain_remediation
description: Pass a GuardVibe rule ID (e.g. VG154) to get a detailed explanation: risk assessment, exploit scenario, minimum fix, secure alternative, and test strategy. Optionally pass the affected code snippet for context-aware guidance. Example: explain_remediation({rule_id: 'VG402'})

name: scan_file
description: Scan a single file on disk by path for security vulnerabilities. Pass a file path — the tool reads the file itself. For inline code snippets, use check_code instead. Example: scan_file({file_path: 'src/api/route.ts'})

name: scan_changed_files
description: Scan only files that have changed since a given git ref (branch, commit, or HEAD~N). Ideal for PR checks, pre-push hooks, and incremental CI. Returns findings only for modified/added files.

name: security_stats
description: Show cumulative security statistics, grade trend, and vulnerability fix progress for this project. Use this to demonstrate the value of GuardVibe security scanning over time. Data is stored locally in .guardvibe/stats.json.

name: audit_mcp_config
description: Scan MCP configuration files (.claude/settings.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json) for security issues: malicious hooks (CVE-2025-59536), suspicious MCP servers, overly permissive tool access, and shell injection patterns. Use this to verify MCP configurations are safe before use.

name: scan_host_config
description: Scan host environment for AI security issues: API base URL hijacking (CVE-2026-21852), credential exposure in shell profiles, .env file leaks, and environment variable sniffing. Checks .env files at project scope; add scope=host to also check shell profiles and global AI configs.

name: guardvibe_doctor
description: Check AI host security: MCP configurations, hooks, base URL hijacking, environment variable exposure. NOT the same as audit_config which checks application config files (next.config, .env, headers). Use scope=project (default) for project-only, scope=host to include shell profiles and global AI configs. Example: guardvibe_doctor({scope: 'project'})

name: verify_fix
description: Verify that a specific security fix was applied correctly. Re-scans the updated code and checks if the target vulnerability (by rule ID) is resolved. Returns 'fixed', 'still_vulnerable', or 'new_issues' status with details.

name: security_workflow
description: Get the recommended GuardVibe tool sequence for your current task. Returns which tools to call, in what order, and with what parameters. Use this when unsure which tool to use. Example: security_workflow({task: 'pre_commit'})

name: auth_coverage
description: Analyze authentication coverage across Next.js App Router routes. Detects auth guards (Clerk, NextAuth, Supabase, custom) and reports protected vs unprotected routes. Pass files array with route file contents and middleware content. Example: auth_coverage({files: [{path: 'app/api/users/route.ts', content: '...'}], middleware: '...'})

name: deep_scan
description: LLM-powered deep security analysis for vulnerabilities that pattern-matching cannot detect: IDOR, business logic flaws, race conditions, stale auth, mass assignment, privilege escalation. Defaults to Claude Haiku 4.5 (~cents per scan); pass `model: 'sonnet'` for deeper analysis at higher cost. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY env var.

name: full_audit
description: Single command that runs ALL checks: code scan (424 rules), secret detection, dependency CVEs, config audit, taint analysis, and auth coverage. Returns PASS/FAIL/WARN verdict with deterministic hash. IMPORTANT: If verdict is FAIL or WARN, you MUST call remediation_plan next to get a section-by-section fix checklist — do NOT skip any section. After fixing, call verify_remediation to confirm ALL sections are addressed. Example: full_audit({path: '.'})

name: remediation_plan
description: Generate a mandatory section-by-section remediation plan from full_audit results. MUST be called after full_audit when verdict is FAIL or WARN. Returns ordered steps for ALL 6 sections (secrets, code, dependencies, config, taint, auth-coverage) with specific tool calls and actions. AI assistants MUST complete every section — skipping sections is not allowed. Example: remediation_plan({path: '.'})

name: verify_remediation
description: Compare before/after audit results to verify ALL sections were addressed. MUST be called after completing remediation to confirm success. Runs a fresh audit and compares against the before snapshot. Explicitly flags skipped sections and refuses to return 'complete' status unless every section is addressed. Pass the before audit hash or let it re-run. Example: verify_remediation({path: '.', before_hash: 'abc123'})

name: growth_session_init
description:
SINGLE session-start call — bundles auth state + external-tool detection (Clay / Crunchbase browser-cookie probes) + skill overrides + verbiflow browser-session probe into one response. Call this as the FIRST tool of every session before rendering anything to the user. Returns { auth, connected_tools, skill_overrides, browser: {verbiflow_signed_in} }.

`browser.verbiflow_signed_in` is a silent SQLite existence probe (no Keychain prompt) that detects whether the user is currently signed into *.verbiflow.com in any Chrome profile. Combine with auth.is_anonymous to decide whether the MCP session was lost vs. genuinely fresh:
  - is_anonymous=true AND verbiflow_signed_in=true → SUGGEST growth_relogin (strong signal: they have a real account, this MCP just lost its token).
  - is_anonymous=true AND verbiflow_signed_in=false → fresh anon user, route through normal claim flow at delivery (growth_claim_account_oauth).
  - is_anonymous=false → already authed, ignore the probe.

name: growth_auth_status
description: Report the current session: anonymous or claimed user, user_id, workspace slug, and the full list of workspaces the viewer belongs to (id, name, slug). Every skill flow should call this first. Use `workspaces` to name the destination when confirming sequence creation — and if length > 1, ask the user which workspace before calling growth_create_sequence_draft.

name: growth_reset_session
description: Nuke the MCP's local anon session and sign in fresh. Use when Supabase rejects the current tokens with "invalid JWT" / "signature invalid" — typically after a Supabase project JWT-key rotation. Creates a brand-new anonymous user; any previous unclaimed anon workspace is orphaned (Supabase sweeps them on its own schedule).

name: growth_claim_account_oauth
description: Preferred claim flow. Returns a one-click URL that hands this anonymous session to the browser and immediately starts Google (or Microsoft) OAuth. After sign-in, the OAuth identity attaches to the SAME user row, so the workspace / sequences / senders the MCP built carry over unchanged. Use this when the user needs to open the web builder or dashboard. Prefer this over growth_claim_account (magic-link) unless the user explicitly asks for email-based claim.

name: growth_claim_account
description: Attach an email to the current anonymous user. Supabase sends a magic link to the provided email; on click, the anonymous user becomes a real user with that email — workspace, sequences, and senders all carry over with no migration. Idempotent: already-claimed users get a fresh magic link. Returns a claim_token the agent can poll via growth_check_claim_status to detect when the user actually clicks the link.

name: growth_check_claim_status
description: Poll the status of a claim_token returned by growth_claim_account_oauth or growth_claim_account. Returns { status: "pending" | "claimed" | "expired", minted_at, claimed_at?, claimed_user_id?, claimed_email? }. Use this to wait for the user to finish OAuth or click their magic link without asking them to confirm. Poll roughly every 20-30s; stop on "claimed" or "expired".

name: growth_relogin
description:
Re-authenticate a user whose MCP session was previously real (claimed) but whose tokens got invalidated server-side (Supabase JWT key rotation, manual revoke, refresh window blown). Returns a one-click URL the user opens; the page does Google/Microsoft OAuth (not linkIdentity), grabs the resulting Supabase session for their EXISTING auth.users row, mints a per-user MCP token, and POSTs it to my local callback so auth.json recovers the same account — workspace, sequences, senders all reappear instantly.

WHEN to call: (a) the user explicitly asks to re-login / says they lost their session, OR (b) a tool call surfaced "Your session has expired or been invalidated by the server" and the current auth.is_anonymous=false (i.e. they HAD a real account before). NEVER call this for a fresh anonymous user who has never claimed — there's no prior account to re-bind to. For anonymous users use growth_claim_account_oauth (creates the account) or growth_claim_account (magic link) instead.

Different from growth_claim_account_oauth: claim is for anon → real conversion (uses linkIdentity, attaches OAuth to current anon user). Re-login is for already-real users who lost their tokens (uses signInWithOAuth, signs into the existing account).

name: growth_write_skill_override
description: Persist a user-specific skill override so it applies to every future session. Call this when the user explicitly corrects a behavior ("never do X", "always use Y") OR when you observe the same preference confirmed twice in a session. Overrides are loaded in growth_session_init and patch the skill automatically. Anonymous users cannot save overrides — check auth.is_anonymous before calling.

name: growth_chrome_run
description:
Drive any site through the user's real Chrome. Opens a tab on `url` if no tab matching the host is already open (no-op when one exists — preserves user state), runs your `js` in it, then returns the post-state HTML and/or markdown plus your script's return value. Use for the long tail of public directories where a typed integration isn't worth it (AICPA peer review, FINRA broker check, NPI registry, state bar listings, FDA Orange Book, EDGAR, etc.).

**Standard scrape loop:** call once with empty `js` (`'return null'`) to get the landing-page HTML → inspect form/table structure → call again with `js` that ticks checkboxes / fills inputs / submits / waits for results → returns post-submit page.

**JS conventions:** wrap in `return` to get a value back. Async OK — `return await fetch(...)` is fine. The return value is JSON-stringified and surfaced in `js_result`. The JS is also where you'd run `await fetch(...)` if you want to hit the site's API directly (cookies, TLS, Cloudflare clearance all ride for free).

**Format param:** `'html'` (default — semantic, has form input names + hidden fields like `__VIEWSTATE`), `'markdown'` (cheaper for the agent to read; loses some semantic info), or `'both'`. Pick markdown when scanning content, html when you need selectors / form names / hidden inputs.

**`incognito: true`** opens the tab in a private window. Use for clean-session anonymous scrapes (no history, no cookies). **Tradeoff:** incognito drops the user's logged-in state, so any auth-walled site fails. Don't combine with sites you need to be signed into.

**Might-get-blocked warning:** if the site uses Cloudflare bot protection, hCaptcha / reCAPTCHA, an interstitial challenge, or sandboxed JS controllers (Pega, Salesforce, ServiceNow, etc.), JS injection may fail or trigger a block. Signs to look for in the response: `html` contains 'Just a moment', 'Access denied', 'cf-browser-verification', '<title>Attention Required'; `js_result` is empty when you expected data; navigation didn't actually fire after `.click()` (the page state didn't change). When that happens, escalate to `growth_chrome_applescript` for OS-level trusted input.

**Prereq (one-time):** Chrome > View > Developer > Allow JavaScript from Apple Events must be ON. The Crunchbase tools auto-flip this; otherwise tell the user to flip the menu item once.

**Same-origin only:** if your `js` does `fetch(otherOrigin)`, browser CORS applies. Open a tab on that origin first.

**Don't poke sensitive tabs uninvited.** If `host_match` could match `mail.google.com`, `slack.com`, `linkedin.com/messaging`, or any site where the agent could send/post/write on the user's behalf — confirm with the user first. Reading public directories needs no confirmation.

name: growth_chrome_applescript
description:
Run raw AppleScript on the user's Mac. The escape hatch for cases where `growth_chrome_run`'s JS injection isn't enough — most often when a site's controllers gate on `event.isTrusted` and reject synthesized clicks (Pega web mashups, Salesforce Lightning, ServiceNow forms, some Cloudflare challenges). System Events sends real OS-level input that pages can't distinguish from the user.

**When to escalate from `growth_chrome_run` to this tool:**
- `.click()` and `dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click'))` don't trigger the action; UI state doesn't change.
- A page-internal global (Pega's `Grids`, etc.) isn't accessible from injected JS.
- You need to send a keystroke (Tab to focus, Enter to submit, ⌘+L to focus address bar, etc.).
- You need to interact with Chrome's own menus / dialogs (not the page DOM).

**Patterns:**
```applescript
-- Send keystroke to the focused Chrome window
tell application "Google Chrome" to activate
tell application "System Events" to keystroke tab
tell application "System Events" to key code 36  -- Enter

-- Click at screen coordinates (derive via JS first: getBoundingClientRect + window position)
tell application "System Events" to click at {x, y}

-- Run JS in a specific tab AND get the result back
tell application "Google Chrome"
  repeat with t in tabs of window 1
    if URL of t contains "aicpa.org" then
      return execute t javascript "document.querySelector('button.next').click()"
    end if
  end repeat
end tell
```

**Pagination loop pattern (Pega-style sandboxed grid):** focus the page → System Events keystroke Tab repeatedly to land focus on the 'Next' button → key code 36 (Enter) to trigger via real keypress → `growth_chrome_run` to scrape the new state → repeat. Or, derive button screen coordinates via `growth_chrome_run` (read `getBoundingClientRect`, add Chrome window's screen position via `tell application "Google Chrome" to bounds of window 1`), then System Events click at `{x, y}`.

**Returns** `{ stdout, stderr }` — AppleScript's last-expression value lands in stdout. Errors raise.

**Power + responsibility:** AppleScript has full machine access. It can quit apps, click anywhere on screen, send keystrokes to whatever window is focused (including `mail.google.com` if Gmail is up). Don't run scripts that could touch the user's other apps without explicit confirmation.

name: growth_chrome_network_log
description:
Monkey-patch a tab's `fetch` + `XMLHttpRequest` to record every request the page makes — useful for reverse-engineering a site's AJAX endpoints. Once you see the actual URL + body the page sends, you can call it directly via `await fetch(...)` inside `growth_chrome_run` and skip pagination clicks entirely.

**Three actions:**
- `'start'` — install the observer in the matching tab. Idempotent (safe to call repeatedly). Optional `filter` substring restricts which requests get logged. Returns `{ js_result: 'started' | 'already_installed' }`.
- `'drain'` — return all entries collected since the last drain (or since start) AND clear the log. Returns `{ entries: [...] }` where each entry is `{ source: 'fetch' | 'xhr', method, url, status, request_body, response_body, started_at, duration_ms }`. Bodies are truncated to `max_body_chars` (default 8000) — bump for larger payloads. Pass `record_headers: true` on `start` to also capture `request_headers` + `response_headers` per entry — handy for reverse-engineering auth/CSRF flows (e.g. LinkedIn Voyager's `x-li-page-instance` + `x-li-track`).
- `'reset'` — clear the log without uninstalling the observer.

**Typical flow:** call `start` with a `filter` (e.g. `"/data/"`, `"api"`) → trigger an action in the page (click Next via `growth_chrome_run` or `growth_chrome_applescript`) → call `drain` to see what the page just fetched. Once you spot the endpoint + body shape, call it directly with `growth_chrome_run` (`await fetch(url, {...})`) — no more clicking.

**Limitation:** the observer survives page navigations within the same origin (no full reload). On a hard reload or a navigation to a different origin, re-call `start`. The patches are non-removable by design (no `stop` action) — they're cheap shims that the page will never notice.

name: growth_list_clay_tables
description: List Clay tables + workbooks the user has access to, using their local browser Clay session. macOS only. Workspace auto-discovered from the cookie unless `workspace_id` is pinned. Pass `query` to search by name (e.g. "fintech") — server-side filter, narrow + fast. Without `query`: returns up to 30 most-recently-opened tables. With `query`: returns ALL matches (no cap). Returns { tables: [{table_id, view_id, name, workbook_id, workbook_name, row_type, last_opened_at, workspace_id, workspace_name}, ...] }. `view_id` is often null in the list response — `growth_import_clay_table` resolves it lazily at import time. On mode: "unsupported", the user has no Clay session in that browser — ask them to log into Clay there, or try the other browser.

name: growth_import_clay_table
description: Export a specific Clay table as CSV using the user's local Clay session, then upload it to the named source node on a sequence draft (creates a staging session — same path the web CSV-upload flow uses). Use after growth_list_clay_tables / growth_parse_clay_table_url has identified the table_id + view_id the user picked. Requires an existing sequence draft with a source node (get source_node_id from growth_get_sequence). Returns { source_run_id, row_count, columns }. For arbitrary customer Clay tables, pass column_mapping when the columns are custom or ambiguous so staging/enrichment can use trusted canonical fields immediately. Surface the row_count to the user. macOS only (Clay cookie read).

name: growth_parse_clay_table_url
description: Parse a Clay table URL (the one the user sees in their browser tab when viewing a table) into its workspace_id / workbook_id / table_id / view_id components. Use this when the workspace has too many tables for growth_list_clay_tables to be useful, OR when the user just wants to use a specific table and has pasted its URL. Does NOT need the browser cookie — pure URL parsing.

name: growth_search_clay_people
description:
Run a Clay People Search using the user's own Clay account (browser session cookies). 

*** WHAT THIS IS: a PERSONA search — finds people who CURRENTLY hold a given title at companies matching firmographics (size / industry / location). Examples: "VPs of Servicing at mortgage companies 51-500 in the US", "DONs at hospice agencies", "Founders at YC W24 cos". 

*** WHAT THIS IS NOT: a HIRING SIGNAL search. If the user's play is "target companies actively hiring for {role}" (job_posting play, hiring-pain trigger), DO NOT use this tool — there is no live-job predicate here, just current title. Use the native `job_posting` audience source (Flage built-in, cleanest), or growth_search_clay_jobs to pull companies with live posts then chain into growth_find_people_at_companies for the right contacts. Confusing persona-search with hiring-signal is a recurring failure mode — read this carefully before picking. 

ASYNC. This call returns within seconds with `{ job_id, status: "running" }`. Clay searches take 4-8 min at typical scale (most of that is Clay streaming rows into the table — not anything we control). The actual work happens in the background; you MUST poll growth_clay_search_status({job_id}) every 15-30s to see progress and get the final CSV. Polling returns `current_rows` while streaming, then `result.csv_path` + sample + columns when complete. 

TWO MODES based on whether a sequence draft is passed: 

• DISCOVERY mode (no sequence_id + source_node_id) — pure search. When complete, status payload contains: { csv_path, sample, row_count, columns, company_domains, table_id, view_id, workbook_id }. Use when the user just wants to see the people (e.g. before committing to an audience, or when joining multiple searches). 

• ATTACH mode (both sequence_id AND source_node_id passed) — runs the search AND stages + promotes the rows as the sequence's audience. When complete, status payload also includes { source_run_id, promote_status, lead_list_id }. Requires an existing sequence draft. 

*** ALWAYS pass `filters.limit_per_company` (default: 5–10). Clay returns every contact that matches your filters — without a per- company cap, a single large company (e.g. JPMorgan in a financial- services search) floods the audience with dozens of contacts and crowds out the smaller companies that matter for the play. 5 for tight personas, 10 for broader ones. There is no global `limit` knob (intentionally — capping the total truncates the audience and hides whether filters are too narrow). 

Both modes save the CSV to $TMPDIR/flage-clay/ and register it in the manifest (growth_clay_list_saved_results). macOS only (Clay cookie read). If the user has multiple Clay workspaces, pass workspace_id explicitly.

name: growth_clay_search_status
description:
Poll the status of a Clay search started via growth_search_clay_people, growth_search_clay_companies, or growth_search_clay_jobs. All three are async and return a `job_id`. Pass that `job_id` here. Returns: 
- `status`: "running" | "complete" | "failed" | "unknown" 
- `message`: short human-readable summary of the current step 
- `current_rows`: rows materialized in Clay so far (during streaming) 
- `log`: last ~40 progress lines with elapsed timestamps 
- `result`: populated when status="complete" — includes `csv_path`, `row_count`, `sample`, `columns`, `company_domains`, `table_id`, `view_id`, etc. For attach mode, also includes `source_run_id`, `promote_status`, `lead_list_id`. 
- `error`: populated when status="failed" 

Cadence: poll every 15-30 seconds while running. A typical search (10-50k rows) takes 4-8 min — most of which is Clay streaming rows. The fastest you can get the CSV is bound by Clay's upstream search throughput, not by polling frequency. Don't poll faster than every 10s — it adds load with no benefit. 

If status="unknown", the job_id never existed or its state was cleaned up (>7 days old). State persists across MCP-server restarts.

name: growth_clay_export_csv
description:
Export an EXISTING Clay table to a CSV on the local filesystem. No sequence required — the CSV path is returned for the model to read or pass into other tools (growth_join_clay_results_by_domain, growth_upload_clay_csv_to_sequence, etc.). 

Pass exactly ONE of the identifier args: 
- `table_id` (+ optional `view_id`; defaults to the table's firstViewId) 
- `table_url` (full Clay app URL — parsed for ids) 
- `job_id` (a previously-completed growth_search_clay_people job — the underlying table_id + view_id are read from the job state file) 
- `table_name` (substring; only works if exactly one table matches in the user's workspace — otherwise this errors with the candidates so the model can disambiguate) 

When to use this vs the other tools: 
- growth_search_clay_people / _companies / _jobs already write a CSV AND return its path — call this AFTER the fact only if you discarded the csv_path or the search completed in a previous conversation. 
- growth_import_clay_table attaches the CSV to a sequence audience — use that when the user wants the data in a sequence draft, not on disk. 

Returns the same shape as discovery-mode search: { csv_path, row_count, columns, sample, company_domains, table_id, view_id, workbook_id }. Typical runtime: 30-90s depending on row count (export + S3 download).

name: growth_search_clay_companies
description:
Run a Clay Company Search (find-lists-of-companies) using the user's own Clay account (browser session cookies). DISCOVERY tool — does NOT stage rows to a sequence. 

ASYNC: returns a `job_id` immediately and runs the search in the background; you MUST poll growth_clay_search_status({job_id}) every 15-30s. When status="complete", the `result` field carries { csv_path, sample, company_domains, table_id, view_id, workbook_id, columns, row_count }. Feed company_domains into growth_search_clay_people's company_identifier[] to find contacts at these companies. 

BEST PRACTICE — semantic_description is the strongest single lever. Treat it like a concept prompt, not a keyword. When the user says "lead enrichment tools" or "find companies like Clearbit", DO NOT pass "lead enrichment" verbatim. Expand it into a rich 1-3 sentence description of what those companies actually do: what they sell, who they sell to, what their product category is called. Example: "B2B SaaS that enriches contact and company records with firmographic, technographic, and behavioral data. Typically sold to sales / marketing teams for prospecting and ABM. Comparable companies: Clearbit, ZoomInfo, Apollo, People Data Labs, Cognism." Clay's ranking is embedding-based — more specific concept text = better look-alikes. 

Combine semantic_description with structural filters (sizes, country_names, technographics_vendors, minimum_member_count) to narrow. locations / locations_exclude accept free-form strings (cities, states, regions) and DO NOT require a search_raw_location flag — that flag is people-search only. macOS only (cookie read).

name: growth_search_clay_jobs
description:
Run a Clay Job-Posting Search (find-lists-of-jobs) using the user's own Clay account. DISCOVERY tool — does NOT stage rows to a sequence. 

ASYNC: returns a `job_id` immediately and runs the search in the background; you MUST poll growth_clay_search_status({job_id}) every 15-30s. When status="complete", the `result` field carries { csv_path, sample, row_count, columns, company_domains, table_id, workbook_id }. Typical use: find companies actively hiring for a role → pipe company_domains into growth_search_clay_people (with a job_title_keywords filter matching the persona) to reach the people doing that role at the hiring companies. 

USE THESE FILTERS (Clay's jobs output is reliable on them):
  - job_title_keywords — the primary signal. Substring match.
  - job_description_keywords — matches text in the posting body.
  - locations — free-form strings. Country (e.g. "United States"), state, metro, or city — Clay fuzzy-matches. Multiple values OR together.
  - min_num_days_since_posted / max_num_days_since_posted — recency window. Use max=30 for "posted in the last month".

AVOID THESE FILTERS (Clay's job data on these is noisy / inconsistent — results drop too aggressively):
  - employment_type (full-time/contract/etc.) — missing / mislabeled on many postings.
  - seniority — Clay infers this heuristically from the title and often gets it wrong. Rely on job_title_keywords instead (e.g. `["senior", "staff"]` or `["vp", "head of"]`).

There is no `limit` knob (intentionally — capping the count would truncate the audience and hide whether the filters are too narrow). Clay returns every matching job posting.

macOS only.

name: growth_join_clay_results_by_domain
description: Join CSVs from a company search, people search, and/or jobs search on the canonical company_domain key (lowercased, www-stripped, path-stripped). Reads the csv_path returned by each growth_search_clay_* call, joins row-by-row on normalized company_domain, writes a merged summary CSV (one row per domain with aggregated people/jobs counts + first-N samples) and a detail JSON file (full nested structure), and returns { csv_path, json_path, row_count, sample, counts }. Use after running 2+ of the growth_search_clay_* tools to see which companies appear across multiple searches (e.g. "which chip-design companies are ALSO hiring security guards?"). Pure client-side — no Clay API calls, no extra credits.

name: growth_clay_list_saved_results
description: List every Clay CSV / JSON saved locally in this session by growth_search_clay_* and growth_join_clay_results_by_domain. Returns a manifest of { path, kind, entity_kind, label, row_count, table_id, workbook_id, saved_at } so the LLM can recall what's on disk without re-running searches. Use when the user asks "what do I have so far?" or when building a join and needing to find the paths of earlier search results. Pure filesystem read — no Clay or backend calls.

name: growth_upload_csv_to_sequence
description:
Stage a CSV file (from ANY source — Clay searches, the join output, a user-provided path, etc.) onto a sequence draft as its audience. Reads csv_path from disk, validates the headers, then runs the same staging + promotion path used by growth_import_clay_table and the web CSV-upload flow. Returns { source_run_id, row_count, columns, promote_status, lead_list_id, column_mapping }. 

VALIDATION — this tool REQUIRES the CSV to have at least one contact identifier column: an email column (email, email_address) OR a LinkedIn URL column (linkedin_url, linkedin_profile, profile_url, etc.). Without one of those, Flage has no way to reach the contacts. The LLM should verify this BEFORE calling the tool — inspect the `columns` field returned by the search tool (or read the CSV header with a file tool) and confirm the user's CSV has email or linkedin_url. If it doesn't, surface the issue instead of calling this — company-only or job-posting CSVs cannot be staged as an audience; they need to be chained through a people search first. 

Use after growth_search_clay_people (discovery mode), growth_join_clay_results_by_domain (if the join CSV has contact columns), or any user-provided CSV on disk. NOT needed when growth_search_clay_people is called in ATTACH mode (sequence_id + source_node_id passed) — that path already stages.

name: growth_check_csv_variable_coverage
description:
Check whether a CSV has values for the template variables ({{first_name}}, {{company_name}}, etc.) used in a sequence's message copy. Call this BEFORE growth_upload_csv_to_sequence so you can warn the user (or pick a different CSV / enrich first) when too many leads are missing fields. 

Pass `variables` as the list extracted from the copy — strip the curly braces, e.g. ["first_name", "company_name", "job_title"]. Returns { total_leads, per_variable_coverage, leads_with_missing, all_have_required, summary }. `per_variable_coverage` gives missing_count + missing_percent per variable; `leads_with_missing` lists row indices + identifier + the variables they lack so you can show the user concrete examples.

name: growth_get_clay_enums
description: Look up valid Clay filter values for a given field. Use this before constructing search filters to get exact string values that Clay accepts. Supports optional keyword search to narrow a large list (e.g. search "software" in industries). Returns the field type, which tools/filters it applies to, total count, and the matching values. Fields: "industries" (applies to company + people industry filters), "countries" (applies to country_names and location_countries_include).

name: growth_join_csv_files
description:
Join two CSV files on a shared column and write the merged result to disk. Pure local operation — no network, no browser session. Default is a LEFT JOIN: every row from the left CSV is kept; matching columns from the right CSV are appended. Use this whenever you have two CSVs about the same entities (e.g. a people CSV with company_linkedin_url + a companies CSV with company_linkedin_url + company_domain + company_name) and you want a single CSV with all the columns. 

Pass `on` when both sides share the same column name; pass `left_on` + `right_on` when the names differ. `normalize_key` handles common normalization gotchas: "linkedin_url" strips /about/, trailing slashes, query strings, and lowercases; "domain" strips https://, www., paths; "lowercase" just lowercases; "none" matches as-is. 

Returns { csv_path, matched_rows, unmatched_left, unmatched_right, columns } so you can immediately see how clean the join was.

name: growth_get_data_source_options
description: Returns the available data source options for a given play, filtered by which tools the user has connected. Call this immediately after the user confirms the play + channel_mix, BEFORE any search. If needs_user_choice is true, show the options and ask the user to pick. If false, proceed silently with the single option returned. Always surface CSV upload as an additional fallback regardless of the result.

name: growth_research_company
description: Deeply research a company by domain — scrapes their homepage for hero copy / customer logos / testimonials, resolves their LinkedIn company page, finds founders, and pulls the last 5 posts from each founder + the company page. Cached 30 days per domain. Blocks up to ~45s for a fresh run; if it's still not done, returns status "running" with a workflow_id so the skill can tell the user to hold on. ALWAYS confirm with the user before calling this tool (never mention cost/credits/quotas to the user — onboarding is free for them).

name: growth_get_company_research
description: Return the latest stored company-research payload for a domain, without waiting. Use when the user returns after a long gap and you want to check whether a previously-kicked-off workflow has completed since.

name: growth_find_investor_portfolio
description: Given a VC firm name (e.g. "Sequoia Capital", "Andreessen Horowitz", "Y Combinator"), return the list of companies they've publicly invested in by scraping the firm's own portfolio page. Used by the "same-investor warm intro" play (see ~/.claude/skills/growth/playbook.md) to build a target list of other companies backed by the user's own investors. Cached 90 days per investor. Confirm with the user before calling (never mention cost/credits — onboarding is free for them).

name: growth_enrich_companies
description:
Bulk-enrich a list of LinkedIn company URLs with firmographic data (name, employee count, industry, HQ, founded year, description). Lightweight wrapper around the company-enrichment pipeline — pick the exact fields you want from the enrichments enum, and the response only contains those fields. Up to 25 URLs per call; sync, completes in 30-90s for typical batches.

INPUT IS LINKEDIN URLS ONLY. If you have domains, call growth_resolve_company_linkedin_urls first to convert them.

Common use: confirming target company size before locking an audience (e.g. "the Clay job search returned Google + Uber alongside real targets — pull employee_count_band on the top 25 to see how many are sub-150-emp"). NEVER auto-filter by size silently — surface the result to the user and let them decide whether the big-co names belong.

name: growth_reconcile_billing
description: Force the user's workspace subscription to re-sync its per-product quantities (email mailboxes, LinkedIn accounts, etc.) against the actual count of connected senders. Call this AFTER the user confirms a Stripe checkout completed, so seats created via MCP pre-payment get billed on the fresh subscription. Also safe to call any time the user reports a billing mismatch ("I connected LinkedIn but it's not on my invoice"). Idempotent and fast — no-op on orgs with no subscription.

name: growth_connect_linkedin_from_cookies
description: Create a real, persistent LinkedIn sender in the user's workspace by reading the user's active LinkedIn session from their local browser. REQUIRES the `browser` arg: "chrome" or "safari" — ask the user which browser they're logged into LinkedIn on before calling this. In gateway mode the configured GROWTH_MCP_BROWSER_PROVIDER is used instead so the cookie read stays inside the scoped gateway browser identity. No extension, no platform visit. The backend connects the account through Unipile and derives the display name + profile URL from the account metadata. Use this when growth_list_senders shows has_linkedin_account === false AND the user has consented to pulling their local LinkedIn session. macOS/Windows only — returns { mode: "unsupported" } elsewhere; skill should fall back to the senders_url flow. Safari extraction requires Claude Code to have Full Disk Access (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access); if the user picks Safari and the call fails with a permissions error, instruct them to grant FDA + restart Claude Code, then retry.

name: growth_create_sender
description: Create a new sender (the identity that does the sending) in the user's workspace. Call this ONLY when growth_list_senders returned an empty array AND the user has given you their first name, last name, and (optionally) email. This is the FIRST step of onboarding a net-new user — it makes a sender row they can then attach a mailbox or LinkedIn account to. After this returns, immediately follow up with one of: growth_connect_linkedin_from_cookies, growth_connect_mailbox_oauth, or growth_connect_mailbox_app_password — do NOT leave the user with a sender that has no channel connected. Returns { sender_id, display_name, primary_email, ... }.

name: growth_move_sender_account
description: Move a single sender_account (mailbox or LinkedIn) from one sender to another within the same workspace. The canonical use-case: merge two duplicate senders for the same human — e.g. the email connect created one sender and an earlier LinkedIn connect created a second — by moving the account from the duplicate onto the primary sender, then deleting the now-empty duplicate. Reversible: call again with the original sender_id to move it back. Doesn't recreate anything, just repoints `sender_accounts.sender_id`. Call growth_list_senders first to pick the `sender_account_id` of the account to move and the `target_sender_id` of the sender to move it onto.

name: growth_get_mailbox_oauth_quote
description: Quote the cost of the next Gmail / Microsoft OAuth mailbox connect for this workspace. Call this RIGHT BEFORE asking the user 'OAuth or app password?" so you can tell them how many free OAuth mailboxes they have left vs. how much the next one will cost. Returns { current_count, free_quota, will_be_charged, price_cents, requires_workspace_subscription, has_workspace_subscription }. Rule of thumb wording: if `will_be_charged === false` → *"OAuth: free, you've used {current_count} of {free_quota} free mailboxes."*. If `will_be_charged === true` → *"OAuth: the next mailbox is ${price_cents/100}/mo (you've already used your {free_quota} free ones)."*. App password is always free regardless — mention that in the same breath so the user can make an informed pick.

name: growth_connect_mailbox_oauth
description: Generate a Unipile hosted-OAuth link the user clicks to connect a Gmail or Microsoft mailbox to an existing sender. Returns { auth_url, provider_link_id, will_be_charged, price_cents }. Send the `auth_url` back to the user verbatim — they open it, authorize in the provider's own UI, and Unipile's webhook creates the sender_account row. Use this when the user wants to connect an email mailbox and has a standard Gmail/Microsoft account (NOT when they're stuck with an IMAP-only / custom-domain account — those need growth_connect_mailbox_app_password). Requires a sender — call growth_create_sender first if growth_list_senders was empty.

name: growth_connect_mailbox_app_password
description: Connect a Gmail mailbox via an IMAP/SMTP app password — the fallback when OAuth won't work (Workspace admin disabled it, custom domain routed through Gmail, etc.). Two steps under the hood (auth/start + provider-links complete); chained here so the agent makes one call. The user must have already generated an app password at https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords (requires 2-step verification enabled). Returns { sender_account_id, identifier, ... } on success. On invalid-password errors, surface the backend message verbatim — it's the user's cue to regenerate the app password and retry.

name: growth_connect_crunchbase
description: Verify the user is signed into Crunchbase in Chrome. Auto-configures the "Allow JavaScript from Apple Events" Chrome policy if it's off (writes the policy via `defaults` + restarts Chrome so it takes effect), opens a crunchbase.com tab if none exists, then calls /v4/cb/sessions to confirm the connected account. On first run the user may briefly see Chrome quit and relaunch — tabs are restored.

name: growth_resolve_crunchbase_entities
description: Translate human names into Crunchbase UUIDs via /v4/data/autocompletes. Works for industries (collection="categories"), broader category groups ("category_groups"), investors ("principal.investors"), companies ("organization.companies"), or locations ("locations"). Returns matched / unmatched / ambiguous buckets. Use when the user names an entity and you need its UUID for a search predicate.

name: growth_search_crunchbase_companies
description: Search Crunchbase for companies matching firmographic filters (industries, category groups, employee size, last-funding date/type/amount, investors). Human names for industries/investors are resolved automatically via autocomplete. Returns a CSV path + sample + next_cursor for pagination. Default `pages: -1` walks all matching pages up to the recommended cap of 20 (= 1000 rows at default `limit: 50`); pass an explicit `pages: N` (max 100) to override the recommended cap when the user has confirmed a bigger pull. Sleeps `sleep_ms` ± 33% jitter between pages (default 1500ms). Stops early when Crunchbase returns no next_cursor; partial results are returned if a mid-loop page errors. To go beyond the recommended cap, either resume with `after_id` or pass an explicit `pages: N`. For a cheap discovery call (just to read `total_matching` before deciding how much to pull), pass `pages: 1`.

name: growth_deanonymize_contacts
