description: Start an async workflow to deanonymize a batch of partial contact records into LinkedIn profiles. For each contact, pass any 2+ of {first_name, last_name, company_name, company_domain, job_title, location}. Internally runs a LinkedIn people-search with first/last name + company (preferred) or job_title (fallback when no company is known); location is intentionally not used as a filter. If `company_domain` is supplied it is resolved to the LinkedIn company URL directly (exact lookup); otherwise `company_name` is resolved via search. If the primary search returns 0 hits, a hailmary retry drops the disambiguator and re-queries with just the name. The LLM picker then chooses the best candidate from up to 3, but `candidates` always carries the full list so the agent can override. Returns {job_id} immediately — poll growth_get_deanonymize_contacts_results to read the resolved profiles. Per-record results cached 14d. Default confidence gate is 60. Hard cap: 50 contacts per call. Never reveal the underlying vendor / actor details to the user; describe behavior only.

name: growth_get_deanonymize_contacts_results
description: Fetch status + results from a deanonymize-contacts job. `finished: false` means the workflow is still running — poll again in a few seconds. `finished: true` and `failed: false` means `results` is the final list (one entry per input contact). Each result has flat top-level fields {found, confidence, linkedin_url, title, full_name, first_name, last_name, company_name, location, reason} pulled out of the LinkedIn search payload — use these directly when building a CSV instead of digging into `profile`. The raw `profile` object is also returned for any field not flattened, and `candidates` carries every profile the search returned (up to 3 from Apify + Serper /in fallback) so you can override the LLM pick if it looks wrong. Title prefers structured currentPosition[0].position over the (often decorated) headline. `failed: true` surfaces `error_message`. `summary` (total/found/not_found/cached/hit_rate) is included only when finished successfully. Results are NOT paginated — the whole batch (≤50) is returned in one call.

name: growth_get_external_tools_used
description: Silently detect which third-party sales tools the user is logged into by checking local browser cookie existence (no decryption, no password prompts, no network calls). Call this in the session-start detection burst — the result GATES which discovery tools are allowed in play-proposal alternatives. macOS only. Currently probes: Clay (chrome / safari), Crunchbase (chrome only). Returns { tools: [{name, present, browser, integrated}, ...] } where `browser` is "chrome" | "safari" | null, and `integrated` is true if we have an actual data-pull integration for that tool today (vs. acknowledgment-only). NEVER surface a tool whose `present` is false in alternatives — that would hallucinate a capability the user hasn't set up.

name: growth_fetch_person_profiles
description: Fetch full LinkedIn person profiles for a list of LinkedIn URLs (e.g. https://www.linkedin.com/in/jane-doe/). Returns the structured profile payload (full_name, headline, currentPosition[], experience[], education[], location, about, etc.) for each URL. S3-cached for 30 days per URL — repeat calls for the same URL are free. Bad/private URLs come back with `found: false`. Use this when you have LinkedIn URLs (from a CSV upload, find_people output, sales_nav export, etc.) and need full profile detail to drive personalization, AI filters, or enrichment. BY DEFAULT also returns each profile's recent posts (past 20 days, authored by THIS profile) on the result's `recent_posts[]` — costs +1 credit per profile, required by the personalization selector for Tier-A signal detection (recent posts, launches, talks). Set `with_recent_posts: false` to skip the post fetch and save the credit when you only need static profile data (e.g. routing / matching). Hard cap: 200 URLs per call. Never reveal vendor/actor details to the user.

name: growth_list_incubator_options
description: List available incubators, or pass incubator_name to list its valid batch_ids. Use before growth_incubator_batch when the exact incubator or batch spelling is uncertain.

name: growth_incubator_batch
description: Data-native incubator batch job. Use when the user wants incubator/batch data back directly, without creating or editing a sequence. result_mode="companies" returns company rows; result_mode="people" finds contacts at those companies with target_title_tags using the same shared engine as the platform incubator source. Returns a composable job_id; poll with growth_get_job and export with growth_export_job_csv.

name: growth_job_posting_contacts
description: Data-native job posting contacts job. Use when the user wants hiring-related job posting and contact rows back directly, without creating or editing a sequence. Runs the same shared engine as the platform job_posting source and exports job_posting, contact, contact_skip, and contact_error rows. Returns a composable job_id; poll with growth_get_job and export with growth_export_job_csv.

name: growth_get_personalization
description:
One-shot personalization for a list of LinkedIn URLs. Replaces the agent-side personalization_selector → personalization_writer subagent chain — call THIS tool instead of spawning subagents. The backend fetches each profile + recent posts (≤ 20-day window), calls gpt-5.4-mini per profile in parallel with the selector/writer/critic rules baked into the system prompt, and regex-verifies the output before returning. 

Mode is implicit:
  • Provide `template` → returns ONE-LINE `personalization_note` for each contact (fits the {{personalization_note}} slot). Pipe results into growth_set_contact_personalization_note() or the CSV column.
  • Omit `template` → returns full bespoke email (`bespoke_subject` + `bespoke_body`) for each contact, suitable for one-off bespoke sends.

SKIP (no qualifying Tier-A signal) returns null fields — that is the correct outcome for most contacts; ship the templated message clean. "No personalization is better than bad personalization." Hard cap: 50 URLs per call. Costs: profile fetch is S3-cached 30d (free on repeats); with_recent_posts adds +1 credit/profile; one gpt-5.4-mini call per profile. Never reveal vendor/actor details to the user.

name: growth_qualify_rows
description: Standalone AI-qualify rows from a local CSV file. Use this when the user already has CSV/list data and wants qualified data back; it does NOT create or edit a sequence. Primary input is csv_path to avoid sending hundreds of rows through chat. Processes at most 500 rows per job. IMPORTANT — chunk size auto-narrows for wide CSVs: the bridge rejects uploads over 5 MiB, so when rows are wide (long pitch / persona / description columns) the tool will use FEWER rows per chunk than max_rows. The response includes a `chunk_size` object with `requested_max_rows`, `effective_max_rows`, `byte_capped`, and a human-readable `reason`. When `byte_capped: true` the `note` explains the narrowing AND the `next_start_row` to continue from — just call again with that start_row, do not fight the narrowing by lowering max_rows yourself. Returns job_id, progress, mapping summary, chunk_size info, and a small preview. Use growth_get_job to poll and growth_export_job_csv to download the result CSV.

name: growth_get_job
description: Get status and a page of rows for any generic composable MCP job, including growth_qualify_rows and growth_targeted_search_people. Use this instead of per-tool status tools when you have a job_id.

name: growth_export_job_csv
description: Download the full CSV artifact for a completed composable MCP job to local disk. Use after growth_get_job shows completed, or call directly and handle "not available yet".

name: growth_targeted_search_people
description: Data-native targeted LinkedIn people search. Use when the user wants people data back directly, without creating or editing a sequence. Filters by job_title_tags, location_tags, and/or LinkedIn company URLs. For large company URL lists such as 500 companies, pass company_linkedin_urls_csv_path instead of inline arrays. Returns a composable job_id; poll with growth_get_job and export with growth_export_job_csv.

name: growth_run_sequence_personalization
description:
Run personalization on a sequence audience — the same flow the in-product "Personalize" button triggers. Two modes:
  • dry_run=true (default): preview on a sample. If `contact_ids` is supplied, those are used (capped by max_contacts). Otherwise the bridge samples max_contacts random contacts from the audience. Nothing is written.
  • dry_run=false: walks the full audience and writes the generated note onto contact_enrichments_jsonb.personalization_note for each contact. `contact_ids` is ignored in this mode.
Returns {workflow_id} immediately — poll growth_get_sequence_personalization_progress until finished:true to read the per-contact results. The personalization config (sender context, value prop, CTA, sequence brief) is read from the sequence itself; no need to pass it in. Default max_contacts is 10 (cap 1000). When the audience is empty or the sequence has no sources, returns `workflow_id: ""` with a `reason` instead of starting a workflow.

name: growth_get_sequence_personalization_progress
description: Snapshot of a personalization workflow started by growth_run_sequence_personalization. Poll repeatedly until `finished: true`. While running, returns the latest `status` ("running"|"pending") and `latest_step` (e.g. "fetching_and_matching", "generating_notes"). When `finished: true` and `failed: false`, `results` is the per-contact list — each row has contact_id, contact_full_name, note (the generated personalization line; empty when SKIP), skipped_reason, written. `failed: true` surfaces `error_message`. `summary` (total/written/skipped/with_note) is included only on successful completion.

name: growth_extract_person_attributes
description:
Extract voice-calibration attributes from LinkedIn profiles for cold-outreach copy. Returns career_stage, generation, register_recommendation, country, and a 1-2 sentence connection_story per profile. It does not return shared-affiliation vectors; use growth_suggest_sender for sender-lead routing.

**Use the result as voice CALIBRATION, never as facts to cite.** The copy writer reads these to shape register / generation / locale / angle, but NEVER quotes attribute values back to the recipient. "I see you went to MIT therefore..." is the canonical anti-pattern — banned. See attribute_extractor.md for the calibration-not-citation rule.

When to call: individual outreach OR small-batch sequence (≤ 20 targets) OR enterprise sequence (≤ 100 targets, where personalization is mandatory). Skip for high-volume SMB sequences (cost + latency not worth it).

sender_context is REQUIRED for sender-aware calibration. Pass at minimum: sender_name, sender_company, sender_role. Add sender_school, sender_company_description, sender_affiliations (e.g. ["YC W22", "ex-Stripe"]) when available.

name: growth_suggest_sender
description:
Pick the best-matched sender from a candidate pool for a given lead. Pass the lead's LinkedIn URL and a list of candidate senders (each with sender_id + their own LinkedIn URL). Returns:

- `result: "matched"` + `suggested_sender_id` — a strong authentic shared affiliation was found. Route the lead to this sender.
- `result: "anyone"` — no strong match. Fall back to the pool's normal strategy (round-robin / weighted / etc.). Do NOT force a match.

The matching uses cached profile attributes + deterministic scoring — fast (subsecond after first cache fill) and proprietary (algorithm lives server-side). The caller never sees per-feature scores or the matching algorithm.

Use cases: per-lead sender routing in sequences, picking the right sender for an individual outreach. The reason_summary is a short plain-language hint for logging/debugging — NEVER cite it back to the recipient (same calibration-not-citation rule as attribute_extractor).

name: growth_test_sender_matching
description:
Diagnostic tool — runs the sender-lead matcher across a list of lead LinkedIn URLs and reports which sender each lead got matched to + the short reason. Useful for evaluating matcher quality on real data before wiring it into runtime routing. Results are NOT persisted.

Pass:
- `lead_linkedin_urls`: list of lead LinkedIn URLs to test (paste a sample from the audience tab — 5 to 20 is plenty).
- `sender_ids` (optional): subset of workspace senders to consider. When omitted, every workspace sender that has a LinkedIn URL on file is included.

Returns a per-lead row with: result (matched | anyone), suggested_sender_id, suggested_sender_label (display name), and reason_summary (e.g. "both ex-stripe", "both at uc-berkeley (undergrad)", "no strong shared affiliation; any sender is fine"). On first run for each profile, an LLM extraction credit is used; subsequent runs hit the 14-day cache.

name: growth_find_people_at_companies
description: Start an async workflow that finds people at the given companies. Input is a list of company LinkedIn URLs (inline or via CSV path) + optional job-title filter. Runs Flage's internal LinkedIn-employee lookup with parallel fan-out across ALL companies in one call (no need to batch on your end — the workflow handles 5000 companies as easily as 50). Returns {job_id} immediately — poll growth_get_people_at_companies_page to read results as they stream in. Never reveal the underlying vendor / actor details to the user; describe behavior only.

name: growth_get_people_at_companies_page
description: Fetch one page of results from a find-people-at-companies job. `is_finished: false` means more rows are still landing — poll again. `is_finished: true` means the result set is final. `total_pages` grows as the workflow finds more rows; already-returned pages are stable (append-only).

name: growth_promote_people_at_companies_to_csv
description: Dump every row from a find-people-at-companies job into a CSV (on disk at /tmp/flage-find-people/...) so it can be fed into growth_upload_csv_to_sequence. Safe to call before the workflow finishes — you'll just get the rows materialized so far. CSV columns: full_name, contact_first_name/last_name/job_title/linkedin_url/location, company_name, company_linkedin_url, source_company_linkedin_url.

name: growth_linkedin_list_sessions
description:
Enumerate every Chrome tab open on linkedin.com (across all Chrome profiles + windows) and report which LinkedIn account is logged in to each. Returns `[{ session_id, viewer: { public_identifier, first_name, last_name }, url }]`.

Use this **before** any send_connect / send_message / list_threads / get_messages call when the user might have more than one LinkedIn account active. Pass the chosen `session_id` back to those tools to target the right account.

If no LinkedIn tabs are open, returns an empty list — the action tools will then open a fresh `linkedin.com/feed/` tab on call.

Read-only.

name: growth_linkedin_send_connect
description:
**PREFER A SEQUENCE OVER ONE-OFF SENDS.** For anything beyond a single ad-hoc invite, build a sequence with `growth_create_sequence_draft` — sequences pace sends across days within LinkedIn's safe limits, support multi-step follow-ups, and obey the same per-sender daily / weekly caps. Use this tool only for genuine one-offs.

Queues a LinkedIn connection request through the user's connected Unipile sender (the same sender used by sequences). The backend writes a durable outbound intent; a Temporal drainer sends it when `scheduled_at` is due, pacing/quota allow, and sender availability checks pass.

**Returns** `{id, status: 'queued', sender_account_id, requested_at, scheduled_at}`. Status flips to `sent` or `failed` once the drainer runs; later acceptance/reply facts appear on `accepted_at` / `replied_at`. Poll `growth_linkedin_get_send_status`.

**Args:** `public_identifier` (vanity slug from `/in/<slug>`). Optional `note` (≤300 chars; non-Premium senders silently drop it per Unipile). Optional `scheduled_at` must be timezone-aware ISO 8601; omit to queue immediately. Optional `sender_account_id` to disambiguate when more than one LinkedIn sender is connected.

**Externally-visible action — confirm with the user before calling.**

name: growth_linkedin_send_message
description:
**PREFER A SEQUENCE OVER ONE-OFF SENDS.** For multi-recipient or multi-step outreach, build a sequence instead. This tool is for single one-off DMs only.

Queues a LinkedIn DM through the user's connected Unipile sender. Backend behavior is identical to `growth_linkedin_send_connect` — durable outbound intent, optional schedule, drainer send, shared per-sender daily / weekly cap with sequence sends.

**Returns** `{id, status: 'queued', sender_account_id, requested_at, scheduled_at}`. Poll `growth_linkedin_get_send_status` for `sent_at`, `failed`, and later `replied_at`.

**Externally-visible action — confirm with the user before calling.** Recipient should already be a 1st-degree connection (Unipile / LinkedIn reject DMs to non-connections from a free account).

name: growth_linkedin_get_send_status
description:
Checks a one-off LinkedIn send created by `growth_linkedin_send_connect` or `growth_linkedin_send_message`. Returns provider-send lifecycle plus engagement fields: `queued`, `sent`, `failed`, `scheduled_at`, `next_eligible_at`, `sent_at`, `accepted_at`, `replied_at`, and `detail`.

Use this for manual one-off sends only. Sequence sends are tracked through sequence/progress tools.

name: growth_linkedin_get_messages
description:
Fetch the message thread with a specific person (or by conversation URN). Pass `public_identifier` and the tool finds the existing 1:1 conversation, or pass `conversation_urn` directly.

**Multi-account safety:** pass `session_id` from `growth_linkedin_list_sessions` when more than one LinkedIn tab is open.

Reads the user's real LinkedIn inbox — confirm before calling.

name: growth_linkedin_list_threads
description:
List the user's recent LinkedIn message threads (inbox). Returns each thread's `entityUrn` (use as `conversation_urn` in `growth_linkedin_get_messages`) and participant names.

**Multi-account safety:** pass `session_id` from `growth_linkedin_list_sessions` when more than one LinkedIn tab is open.

Reads the user's real LinkedIn inbox — confirm before calling.

name: growth_linkedin_get_post
description:
Fetch a LinkedIn post by URL (`https://www.linkedin.com/posts/...`), feed-update URL, raw `urn:li:activity:N`, or just the numeric id. Hits Voyager `/feed/updates/<urn>` from the user's logged-in Chrome tab — same approach as the post-reactor audience source uses, but for one specific post on demand.

Returns `{ urn, text, author: { name, public_identifier }, counters: { reactions, comments, reposts } }`. Read-only, **does not** count toward the LinkedIn write cap.

**Multi-account safety:** pass `session_id` from `growth_linkedin_list_sessions` when more than one LinkedIn tab is open. Auto-picked when only one tab is open.

name: growth_linkedin_search_posts
description:
Search LinkedIn posts (the same content search you get at `linkedin.com/search/results/content/`) via the user's connected LinkedIn sender. Powered by Unipile classic search (`api: classic, category: posts`).

**Sender selection:** auto-picks when only one connected LinkedIn sender exists. Otherwise pass `sender_account_id` (the `senders.accounts[].id` from `growth_list_senders`) to choose which account performs the search.

**Filters** mirror the LinkedIn UI filter panel:
- `keywords` — search query.
- `date_posted` — `past_24h` | `past_week` | `past_month`.
- `content_type` — `videos` | `images` | `live_videos` | `job_posts` | `documents`.
- `sort_by` — `date` (latest) | `relevance` (top match).
- `posted_by` — `me` | `my_network` | `1st_connections` | `following`.
- `from_member` — array of LinkedIn member identifiers (vanity slug or URN).
- `from_company` — array of LinkedIn company identifiers (vanity slug or URN).
- `author_keywords` — restrict to posts whose author headline matches (e.g. `"CEO"`).
- `extra_filters` — passthrough object for any other Unipile field.

**Pagination:** pass `cursor` from the previous response to page. `limit` caps results per call (Unipile classic max: 50).

Read-only — does NOT count toward the LinkedIn write hourly cap. Returns `{ items, cursor, sender_account_id, unipile_account_id }`.

name: growth_linkedin_search_people_start
description:
Kick off a paginated LinkedIn classic-people search (the same people search you get at `linkedin.com/search/results/people/`) as a background Temporal job. Returns a `job_id` immediately — DO NOT block; poll `growth_linkedin_search_people_get_page` until `is_finished=true` (or read partial results as pages come in).

Powered by Unipile (`api: classic, category: people`). Page size is fixed at 10 (Unipile classic cap). Workflow sleeps 3-4s between page fetches to mimic human pacing — a 15-page run takes roughly 45-75s wall clock.

**Sender selection:** auto-picks when only one connected LinkedIn sender exists. Otherwise pass `sender_account_id` (the `senders.accounts[].id` from `growth_list_senders`).

**Filters:**
- `keywords` — search query (boolean modifiers supported, e.g. `growth AND lead NOT manager`).
- `network` — array of LinkedIn network-distance codes: `F` (1st-degree), `S` (2nd-degree), `O` (3rd+/out-of-network). Example: `["S"]` matches the LinkedIn URL `?network=%5B%22S%22%5D`.
- `location` — array of place names. Mapped to LinkedIn `geoUrn` IDs server-side. Currently supported:
    *Countries:* France, Belgium, Spain, England, Germany, Italy, United States, Canada, Australia, India, China, Japan, Brazil, Mexico, Netherlands, Singapore, Switzerland, Sweden, South Korea, Russia, United Arab Emirates.
    *US metros / cities / states:* San Francisco Bay Area, San Francisco, California, United States; New York City Metropolitan Area; New York, United States; Boston, Massachusetts, United States.
    Use the most specific name that matches the user's intent. For any place not on this list, pass the LinkedIn geo ID directly via `extra_filters: { location: ["<id>"] }`.
- `extra_filters` — passthrough object for any other Unipile field (industry, current_company, school, etc.) or extra location IDs.

Returns `{ job_id, workflow_id, sender_account_id, unipile_account_id }`. Read-only — does NOT count toward the LinkedIn write hourly cap.

name: growth_linkedin_search_people_get_page
description:
Read a page of results from a LinkedIn people-search job started via `growth_linkedin_search_people_start`. Each call returns up to `page_size` people plus a status snapshot.

**Polling pattern:**
1. Call `growth_linkedin_search_people_start`, save `job_id`.
2. Call this tool with `job_id, page=1` every ~5s until `is_finished=true`. Partial results are visible during the run — `pages_fetched` tells you how far the workflow has progressed (out of `pages_planned`).
3. When `total_count > page_size`, increment `page` to drain the rest.

Returns `{ people, page, page_size, total_count, total_pages, pages_fetched, pages_planned, is_finished }`. If the workflow `failed`, `is_finished=true` with `error_message` populated via `/status` (call `growth_linkedin_search_people_get_page` first; if zero results and finished, the search hit an error — surface it to the user).

name: growth_linkedin_get_contact_relationship
description:
Look up a LinkedIn person from the connected sender's vantage point. Returns name, headline, location, occupation, **network distance** (`SELF` / `DISTANCE_1` = 1st-degree connection / `DISTANCE_2` / `DISTANCE_3` / `OUT_OF_NETWORK`), `is_connection` boolean (true iff 1st-degree or self), and an `id` you pass to `growth_linkedin_get_chat_history` for past message history.

**Sender selection:** auto-picks when only one connected LinkedIn sender exists. Otherwise pass `sender_account_id`.

**Use this BEFORE sending a connect / DM** to know whether you're already connected (skip the connect, go straight to DM) or 2nd-degree (connect first), and to ground any claim about the person in real profile data instead of guessing from a slug.

Powered by Unipile's `GET /users/{public_identifier}` endpoint. Read-only, doesn't count toward the LinkedIn write hourly cap.

name: growth_linkedin_get_chat_history
description:
List every message the connected sender has exchanged with this person across all 1:1 LinkedIn chats. **`items[0]` is the most recent message.** Each message carries `text`, `timestamp` (ISO 8601), `is_sender` (1 = we sent it, 0 = they sent it), `chat_id`, `attachments`, `message_type` (MESSAGE / INVITATION / INMAIL / etc.), and `seen` status.

**Pagination:** auto-drains up to 5 pages × 250 messages = 1250-message ceiling per call (one second pacing between pages). LinkedIn 1:1 chats almost never exceed that. If you genuinely need to go deeper, pass `cursor` from a previous response to resume.

**`id`** must be the `id` returned by `growth_linkedin_get_contact_relationship` (LinkedIn member URN — Unipile accepts it as `provider_id`).

**Use this after `get_contact_relationship`** to see whether you've talked before, what was said, and how recent the last touch was — gives the agent the full conversation context before deciding to follow up vs. cold-DM vs. skip.

Returns `{ items, cursor, pages_fetched, sender_account_id, unipile_account_id }`. Empty `items` = no chat history with this person.

name: growth_resolve_company_linkedin_urls
description:
Resolve a list of company domains to their LinkedIn company URLs (e.g. acme.com -> https://www.linkedin.com/company/acme). Runs an async backend workflow that resolves each domain to its company page on LinkedIn. Polls until finished, then returns a 4-column bridge CSV (company_domain, company_linkedin_url, source, status).

Use this whenever you have domains (Clay jobs CSV, Crunchbase export, manual list, etc.) and need real LinkedIn URLs to feed into growth_find_people_at_companies — guessing slugs from company names silently drops 10-25% of rows. To carry domain + name through to the final people CSV, then pass the bridge CSV through growth_join_csv_files (left = bridge, right = people CSV, on=company_linkedin_url, normalize_key=linkedin_url).

name: growth_resolve_company_domains
description:
Resolve a list of company names to their canonical website domains. For each name, the workflow searches the web, drops aggregator and directory hosts (linkedin, yelp, wikipedia, indeed, glassdoor, crunchbase, bbb, ...), then picks the candidate that is the company's actual website (or "none" if no candidate clearly belongs to that firm). Polls until the workflow finishes, then returns a 6-column bridge CSV (company_name, company_location, company_domain, source, status, matched_url).

Use this whenever you have a list of company names without domains. The tool is upstream-agnostic: works for names from a CSV upload, a Chrome scrape of a public directory, a Clay search, a manual list, anywhere. `location` (city / state / country) is OPTIONAL — pass it for common firm names ("Smith & Co LLP") to disambiguate, skip it for unique names ("Stripe", "Datadog") where it adds nothing. Don't fabricate location; a wrong location is worse than none. Up to 2000 companies per call.

name: growth_get_sequence_template
description: Return a canonical sequence template. Call this BEFORE drafting copy. Pass `channel_mix` to pick the shape: `mix` (default, branched email+LinkedIn), `email_only` (3-touch email cadence, no LinkedIn), `linkedin_only` (connection request + post-accept DM, no email). The agent should ALWAYS ask the user up front which mix they want before fetching the template — default to `mix` unless they say otherwise. Returns the step shape + slot_rules + copy guardrails. Fill slots by asking the user targeted questions (never invent answers), then call growth_create_sequence_draft. Allowed {{var}} names: first_name, last_name, company_name, sender_first_name, sender_last_name, sender_company_name, personalization_note.

name: growth_ensure_workspace
description: Ensure the current user has a workspace. Creates one if this is a brand-new anonymous user. Returns the workspace slug. Safe to call repeatedly. Pass `workspace_id` (id or slug) to switch the active workspace context — subsequent tool calls in this session will route to that workspace.

name: growth_list_sequences
description: List all sequences in the current workspace.

name: growth_get_plans
description: Return the purchasable Verbiflow plan catalog (Starter / Pro / Scale) with current pricing, bundled seats, and credit caps. No auth required and no Stripe round-trip — safe to call before the user has a workspace or to answer "what plans do you have?" directly. Source of truth is backend `PLAN_CONFIG`, so prices stay in sync if they change. Response: { plans: [{ plan_tier, display_name, price_cents, bundled_seats, credits_limit }], default_plan_tier }.

name: growth_billing_status
description: Check the current workspace's plan tier and subscription state. Call this silently right before publishing a sequence (not earlier — no need to nag users who are still drafting). Response includes: { has_workspace_subscription: bool, workspace_subscription_status, plan_tier: "free" | "legacy" | "starter" | "pro" | "scale" | null, plan_display_name, plan_bundled_seats, plan_credits_limit, purchasable_plans: [{ plan_tier, display_name, price_cents, bundled_seats, credits_limit }] }. If `plan_tier === "free"` the user has never paid — they cannot publish a sequence. Show them `purchasable_plans`, ask which one fits (Starter / Pro / Scale), then call `growth_get_checkout_url` with that `plan_tier` and hand them the Stripe link.

name: growth_get_checkout_url
description: Generate a Stripe Checkout URL for the current workspace subscription on a specific plan tier. Use this when `growth_billing_status` reports `plan_tier === "free"` (or no active subscription) AND the user has told you which plan they want. Returns `{ checkout_url }` — hand that URL to the user verbatim; one click opens hosted Stripe checkout, and after success Stripe redirects them back to `success_url`. Optional `promo_code` applies a discount.

name: growth_list_senders
description: Return the viewer's senders + their channel accounts. A sender is the person/identity doing the sending; each sender has one or more accounts (email mailbox, LinkedIn account). Use this to decide whether the user needs to connect an email mailbox or LinkedIn before publishing / sandbox-sending. Response shape: array of { sender_id, display_name, email, accounts: [{ channel: "email"|"linkedin", provider, connection_status, health_status, ...}] }. A fully-connected email account has connection_status !== "disconnected" / "not_connected". Call this silently before prompting the user to connect — only ask if the relevant channel is actually missing, and return the builder senders URL for them to connect via the web UI.

name: growth_list_audience_sources
description: Return the live registry of audience source kinds Flage supports + the attributes each emits per lead. ALWAYS call this before proposing an ICP or picking a source_kind for growth_create_sequence_draft — the list is the authoritative ground truth, hardcoding sources in the skill goes stale. Response shape: { sources: [{kind, default_display_name, description, default_config, output_columns: [{field_key, display_name}], ui_state, ...}], enrichment_attributes: [{key, attribute_type, note}], unsupported_facets: [string] }. Use `output_columns` + `enrichment_attributes` to decide what filters are possible. If the ICP requires a facet in `unsupported_facets` (funding_stage, revenue, tech_stack, etc.), DO NOT propose it unless the user explicitly asks.

name: growth_get_sequence
description: Full detail of a sequence — name, state, steps, lead count, metrics, and web_url.

name: growth_create_sequence_draft
description: Create a new sequence draft. Pass a name, an ordered list of steps, and optionally the audience source. Each step has channel (email | linkedin_connection | linkedin_message), body, subject (email only), wait_hours (delay before this step). LinkedIn connection-request steps can branch via on_accepted (continues on LinkedIn) and on_not_accepted (falls back to email). audience_source picks the right lead pipeline: incubator (YC), linkedin_post_reactors, linkedin_network, job_posting, targeted_search, conference_attendees, sales_nav_url, luma_events, or manual (CSV fallback). Never ship "manual" if a better source fits the ICP.

name: growth_update_sequence_steps
description: Replace the email / LinkedIn step chain on an existing sequence draft. Use this AFTER growth_create_sequence_draft whenever you rewrite copy with the user — edits in chat are not persistent until you call this tool. The audience source, filter prompt, sender selection, and schedule are preserved untouched; only the step chain is rebuilt. Optimistic concurrency is handled internally (tool reads draft_version before writing), so the agent just passes the new steps. Steps use the same shape as growth_create_sequence_draft: channel, subject (email only), body, wait_hours, on_accepted / on_not_accepted branches. Returns the refreshed sequence detail + web_url.

name: growth_update_source_config
description: Patch the config on an existing source node ingress — used to edit source-specific fields like `job_title_tags` (job_posting), `batch_id` / `target_title_tags` (incubator), `query` / `interaction_types` (linkedin_post_reactors), `keyword_tags` / `from_date` / `to_date` (conference_attendees), `job_title_tags` / `location_tags` / `company_linkedin_urls` (targeted_search), etc. Accepts a PARTIAL patch: keys you pass override the current ingress config, keys you omit are preserved from the existing config. The tool reads the current source node via growth_get_sequence, merges your patch, and PATCHes the full merged config back. Auto-picks the source_node_id and ingress_id when the sequence has exactly one active source / ingress — pass them explicitly only when there are multiple. Pass `source_kind` in the config to swap the ingress to a different kind (e.g. job_posting → manual for CSV Import). When swapping kinds, pass only the fields valid for the new kind — stale keys from the old kind will be dropped by the backend schema.

name: growth_delete_sequence_lead_list
description: Detach an uploaded lead list (CSV import) from a sequence draft. Use when a stale or wrong list is still attached alongside the current audience — e.g. an old big-co list left over from an earlier upload. Resolves the lead_list_id from the sequence (call growth_get_sequence first to see attached lists if you don't already have the id). Sequence must be in draft state; published sequences must be edited in the builder. Returns the remaining lead_list_ids so you can confirm the right one was removed.

name: growth_set_personalization_note
description:
Write a per-recipient `personalization_note` value onto a sequence row. AUTO-ROUTES based on which identifiers you pass:
  • Pass `contact_id` → writes to the materialized contact_row (after the source has run / been materialized).
  • Pass `source_run_id` + `row_identifier` → writes to the staging row (BEFORE the source has materialized — used for incubator pulls, linkedin_post_reactors, hiring-signal sources, or manual CSV pre-publish where contacts don't exist yet but you have preview rows).
In both cases, the value flows into `audience_attributes` at enrollment time and becomes the `{{personalization_note}}` template variable at send time. Pass an empty string to clear the slot — the runtime substitutes "" and the surrounding paragraph collapses cleanly.

Important: edits made AFTER a contact is enrolled will NOT affect the in-flight sequence for that contact — the per-instance audience_attributes snapshot is frozen at enrollment time. Set personalization BEFORE publish, or re-enroll the contact afterward to refresh.

name: growth_publish_sequence
description: Publish a sequence — flips from draft to active. MUST have been previewed by the user in chat first. Will fail if no connected mailbox / LinkedIn.

name: growth_run_source_preview
description: Run a source preview (sample mode) on an audience source block and wait for the result. Triggers the same Temporal workflow the builder UI fires when you click Preview, then polls until the source run reaches a terminal state and returns the saved preview rows. Intended for iterative prompt / filter work: run the source once, then call growth_run_ai_filter_preview as many times as you want against the saved preview. Returns { source_run_id, status, mode, row_count, rows }. Each row has row_identifier + row_value (the flat contact payload — name, company, enrichments, source-carried fields). Sample preview caps at a small number of contacts so runs finish in seconds; use the web builder for full runs.

name: growth_run_ai_filter_preview
description: Run an AI filter prompt against the already-saved source preview (sample mode) and wait for the result. Requires that growth_run_source_preview (or the builder UI) has already run the source — this tool does NOT re-pull the source, it only scores the cached preview contacts. Returns { passed_count, failed_count, prompt_hash, rows } where each row has ai_filter_pass (bool), ai_filter_reason (the evaluator LLM's one-line justification), plus the full flattened contact payload. Use this for iterating on a prompt: call it, read reasons on rejected / accepted rows, adjust the prompt, call again — each iteration is cheap since the source preview is reused.

name: growth_update_ai_filter_prompt
description: Persist an AI filter prompt to the sequence draft so it is visible in the builder. Call this after iterating with growth_run_ai_filter_preview and landing on a prompt you are happy with. Reads the current draft_id and draft_version automatically, then PATCHes the filter node in the draft. Returns the persisted prompt and new draft_version.

name: growth_create_organization
description: Create a new Verbiflow workspace (organization) for the current user. Triggers the same onboarding as web signup: starter sequence templates are seeded synchronously, and an `OnboardingPersonalizationWorkflow` runs in the background to personalize them. The caller is added as a member, but the local MCP context (current `org_slug`) is NOT switched — subsequent tool calls keep operating against the workspace you were in before. Use this when the user wants a new workspace, or right before `growth_transfer_sequence` if they need a destination workspace that does not exist yet. Returns `{ org_id, org_slug, viewer_sender_id, starter_template_ids }`.

name: growth_transfer_sequence
description: Move a sequence from the caller's current workspace to a target workspace the caller is also a member of. Moves: the sequence definition, all drafts and revisions, the lead lists + contacts attached to it, and the source-run history. Does NOT move: senders / mailbox auth (OAuth tokens are bound to the source org and would collide on UNIQUE(org, channel, identifier) in target — user must reattach senders in target via the builder), and vendor-side resources (Clay tables, Crunchbase saved searches stay in the user's vendor account; if the target workspace has the same vendor connected, configs resolve fine; otherwise sources sit dormant until reconnected). Pre-flight: caller must be a member of both workspaces (else 403 — call `growth_create_organization` first if the target does not exist), and the sequence must be inactive or paused (active sequences refuse to move so in-flight workflows do not straddle the org boundary). Sequence ASSIGNMENTS (workspace members the sequence was assigned to) are cleared because target-org members may differ. Returns `{ ok, sequence_id, target_org_slug, moved_lead_list_ids, moved_source_run_count, note }`.

name: growth_sandbox_send_test_email
description: Send a real email to the user's own inbox using Flage's shared warmed sandbox sender. Proves sending works before they connect their own mailbox. Subject + body are composed by Claude. Recipient is the user's email. Rate-limited.

name: growth_verify_copy
description: Stage 1 mechanical gate for a sequence draft. Deterministic regex only — catches em-dashes, banned phrases ("hope you're well", "circling back", "just wanted to"), bracket placeholders ([Sender], [calendar link]), begging in commercial mode ("would love", "worth 15 min", "happy either way"), invented template vars like {{burner_domain}}, missing personalization, over-length subjects/bodies, missing \n\n paragraph breaks, LinkedIn note > 300 chars, signature blocks in body, connection-request-without-branches, branch not last outer step. Fast, cheap, no LLM call. Qualitative review (hook nod test, CTA quality, breakup strength, cohort/proof grounding) is NOT done here — that is the critic-subagent system's job (see the growth skill's critic.md, hook_critic.md, breakup_critic.md, linkedin_critic.md). Returns {overall_score (0-10), rating, pass (bool), critical_count, suggestions, per_step_scores, instructions}. pass is true only when zero criticals AND score ≥ 7. If pass is false, apply suggestions in severity order (critical > high > medium > low) and re-run. When pass=true, hand the draft to the critic subagents in parallel — do NOT skip that stage. sender_context and target_context are accepted for forward-compat but currently unused by the regex pass.

name: growth_search_domain
description: Check whether a single domain is available to register and what it costs. Returns { available, banned, registration_price, renewal_price }. The price already includes the $3 markup over InboxKit's wholesale price. Use BEFORE growth_create_mailbox_order to confirm the user-picked domain is purchasable.

name: growth_suggest_domains
description: Generate domain suggestions tied to the current workspace name. Backed by an LLM call against the workspace name + company description. Returns up to ~100 candidate domains, each with `available: null` until the user (or growth_search_domain) checks. Cached 14 days per workspace to avoid repeat LLM cost. Already-known-unavailable domains are filtered out of the response. Use this when the user hasn't named a domain yet and wants suggestions; show them the top ~10 and let them pick.

name: growth_list_purchased_domains
description: List the domains this workspace already owns (purchased through Verbiflow), with their existing mailboxes + remaining capacity (max 5 per domain). Use BEFORE growth_create_mailbox_order to check if the user can attach mailboxes to an existing domain instead of registering a new one (cheaper, faster).

name: growth_create_mailbox_order
description:
PAID ACTION — only call after explicit user confirmation. Creates a billing-intent group for one domain + 1–10 mailboxes. The worker fans out InboxKit provisioning + Stripe charges asynchronously. Returns `{order_group_id, intents}` immediately; poll the order-events stream or refresh growth_list_purchased_domains for fulfillment progress.

Required fields:
  - domain: the registered domain. Must match the @-suffix of every mailbox email.
  - is_new_domain: true if domain needs to be registered (adds a domain purchase intent + registration cost). false if domain is already owned by the workspace.
  - registration_years: 1-10. Only meaningful when is_new_domain=true.
  - mailboxes: array of {email, first_name, last_name, platform}. Min 1, max 10. Default platform: GOOGLE.

NOTE on pricing: the backend looks up the domain registration cost from InboxKit at order-creation time (with the standard $3 markup). You do NOT pass `domain_cost` — it is derived server-side. Use growth_search_domain beforehand to show the user the price for confirmation.

Confirm the proposed order with the user BEFORE calling — once submitted the InboxKit provisioning is async and refunds require manual support.

name: growth_apollo_lookup_phone_start
description: Start a phone-number lookup via Apollo using a person's Apollo ID or LinkedIn URL. Apollo delivers phones asynchronously to our webhook (typically within a few minutes), so this returns immediately with `status: "pending"` and identity/firmographic fields. Use `growth_apollo_lookup_phone_status` with the returned `lookup_id` to fetch the phones once delivered. Requires an Apollo API key connected in the Integrations tab. Consumes Apollo phone credits when the webhook delivers.

name: growth_apollo_lookup_phone_status
description: Fetch the current status + result of a phone lookup started via `growth_apollo_lookup_phone_start`. Returns `status: "pending"` if Apollo has not yet delivered the phones to our webhook, `"complete"` with `phone_numbers` populated once delivered, or `"failed"` with an error message. Apollo waterfall delivery typically takes seconds to a few minutes; safe to poll every 10–30s.

name: literature.search
description: Search PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, bioRxiv/medRxiv, ChEMBL, FDA Orange Book, FDA Purple Book, enterprise sources (Embase, ScienceDirect, Cochrane, Citeline, Pharmapendium, Cortellis), HTA cost reference sources (CMS NADAC, PSSRU, NHS National Cost Collection, BNF, PBS Schedule), LATAM sources (DATASUS, CONITEC, ANVISA, PAHO, IETS, FONASA), APAC sources (HITAP), and HTA appraisal/guidance sources (NICE TAs, CADTH CDR/pCODR, ICER, PBAC PSDs, G-BA AMNOG, HAS Transparency Committee, IQWiG, AIFA, TLV Sweden, INESSS Quebec) for evidence on a drug or indication. Returns structured results including HTA precedents and appraisal decisions with a full audit trail suitable for HTA submissions.

name: models.cost_effectiveness
description: Build a cost-utility analysis (ICER, QALY, PSA, sensitivity analysis) for a drug vs comparator. Follows ISPOR good practice guidelines and NICE reference case. Includes probabilistic sensitivity analysis (PSA), one-way sensitivity, and cost-effectiveness acceptability curve (CEAC). NOTE: utility inputs are value-set-dependent — UK submissions in 2026+ will transition from DSU 3L→5L mapping to the new UK EQ-5D-5L value set (NICE consultation 2026-04-15 to 2026-05-13). Use utility_value_set tool to check expected impact on ICER before finalising inputs.

name: hta.dossier
description: Structure evidence into HTA body-specific submission format (NICE STA, EMA, FDA, IQWiG, HAS, EU JCA, or Global Value Dossier). Produces draft sections with gap analysis and auto-GRADE evidence quality tables. Accepts output from literature.search and models.cost_effectiveness. Enum values are case-insensitive — `"NICE"`/`"nice"`, `"STA"`/`"sta"` etc. all work.

name: knowledge.search
description: Search a project's knowledge base (raw/ and wiki/) for text matches. Returns file paths with line numbers and snippets. Use this to find previously-retrieved literature, model runs, and compiled wiki content without re-querying external APIs.

name: knowledge.read
description: Read a file from a project's raw/ or wiki/ tree. Path is relative to project root. Only raw/ and wiki/ subtrees accessible.

name: knowledge.write
description: Write a file to the project's wiki/ tree. Path MUST start with 'wiki/' and end with '.md'. Use this to compile/organize evidence from raw/ files into a structured knowledge base. Supports Obsidian-style [[wikilinks]].

name: project.create
description: Initialize a new HEOR project workspace with directory skeleton and project.yaml metadata. Idempotent — returns existing project if already created. Required before using the `project` parameter in other tools. Enum values are case-insensitive — `"NICE"`, `"Nice"`, and `"nice"` all work for hta_targets.

name: evidence.network
description: Analyze literature search results to build an evidence network map. Extracts intervention-comparator pairs from titles and abstracts, constructs a treatment comparison network, and assesses NMA (network meta-analysis) feasibility. Pass the results array from a prior literature.search call.

name: evidence.indirect
description: Compute indirect treatment comparisons using the Bucher method (single common comparator) or frequentist network meta-analysis (full network). Requires user-supplied effect sizes (point estimates + 95% CI) from published trials. Supports MD, OR, RR, HR. Auto-selects method by network structure. When direct head-to-head A-vs-C evidence is also in the network, automatically tests Bucher's consistency assumption (z = (direct − indirect) / SE_diff) per NICE DSU TSD 18 / Cochrane 11.4.3 — flags |z|≥1.96 as 'substantial inconsistency' so the agent can warn the user before relying on the indirect estimate.

name: models.budget_impact
description: Estimate the total budget impact of adopting a new intervention over 1-5 years. Follows ISPOR Budget Impact Analysis good practice guidelines (Mauskopf 2007, Sullivan 2014). Computes year-by-year net cost to payer, including market share uptake, treatment displacement, and population growth.

name: evidence.population_adjusted
description: ⚠️ EXPERIMENTAL / orientation-only. Approximate population-adjusted indirect comparison using summary-level statistics (mean, SD per covariate). True MAIC/STC per NICE DSU TSD 18 requires individual patient data (IPD) for one trial. This tool inflates the SE of a Bucher indirect comparison based on covariate imbalance (MAIC-style ESS penalty) and applies a simple linear adjustment based on standardized mean differences (STC-style). Point estimates should be interpreted as approximate — not submission-ready. For a definitive analysis, use IPD with an outcome regression model.

name: evidence.survival
description: Fit parametric survival distributions (Exponential, Weibull, Log-logistic, Log-normal, Gompertz) to either patient-level event-time data (preferred — true right-censored MLE per Collett 2015 / NICE DSU TSD 14) OR Kaplan-Meier step-summary data (legacy approximation, used when only published KM digitization is available). Returns AIC/BIC model comparison and extrapolation table. Supply EXACTLY ONE of `event_data` (patient-level rows) or `km_data` (KM table).

name: literature.screen
description: Screen literature search results using PICO criteria. Scores each abstract by relevance to the research question, classifies study design, and returns a ranked shortlist with inclusion/exclusion decisions and reasons. Pass the results array from a prior literature.search call (use output_format='json'). Follows Cochrane Handbook Chapter 4 screening methodology.

name: evidence.risk_of_bias
description: Assess risk of bias for a set of studies using the appropriate Cochrane instrument: RoB 2 (RCTs), ROBINS-I (observational studies), or AMSTAR-2 (systematic reviews/meta-analyses). Instrument is auto-detected from study_type or can be specified. Judgments are inferred from abstract text — domains without sufficient reporting are marked Unclear. Returns a per-study table and a rob_results object to pass to hta_dossier_prep for evidence-based GRADE assessment. Accepts `studies` as a single object OR an array; auto-wraps singletons. Enum values are case-insensitive — `"RoB2"`/`"rob2"`, `"AUTO"`/`"auto"` all work.

name: utils.validate_links
description: Validate URLs by making HEAD requests and checking HTTP status codes. Returns categorization: working (200), browser_only (403 from bot-blocking sites that work in browsers), broken (404/410), or timeout/error. ALWAYS use this before presenting reference links to users — broken links destroy trust. Pass all URLs you plan to cite.

name: hta.utility
description: Look up EQ-5D value set characteristics (UK 3L, England 5L, new UK 5L 2026, NICE DSU mapping) or estimate the ICER/QALY impact of the new UK EQ-5D-5L value set for a given indication type. Cites Biz, Hernández Alava, Wailoo (2026) Value in Health. Use when user asks about NICE 5L transition, UK utility value sets, or impact on NICE STA submissions.

name: evidence.itc
description: Assess the feasibility of an indirect treatment comparison (ITC) by walking through the three core assumptions (exchangeability, homogeneity, consistency) and recommending an appropriate method: direct comparison, Bucher, full NMA, anchored MAIC/STC, unanchored MAIC/STC, ML-NMR, NMR/subgroup meta-regression, or infeasible. Cites Cope 2014 (BMC Med), NICE DSU TSD 18 (Phillippo), Signorovitch 2023 (J Dermatol Treatment), and Cochrane Handbook Ch 10-11. Use this BEFORE running evidence.indirect or evidence.population_adjusted to select the right method.

name: examples
description: Get a pre-filled, copy-runnable JSON input for any of the heavy-schema tools (cost_effectiveness_model, budget_impact_model, survival_fitting, population_adjusted_comparison, evidence_indirect). Use when you want to demo a tool but don't want to invent inputs from scratch — the example is editable so you can tweak intervention names, costs, populations, etc. before calling the actual tool.

name: workflow.maic
description: Run the canonical MAIC discovery+screening pipeline in one call: ITC feasibility + parallel literature_search (broad + per-trial) + PICO screening + risk_of_bias + evidence_network. Stops short of running MAIC/Bucher itself (those require IPD or trial-level effect estimates). Produces a structured 9-section report with explicit Next Steps. Use this as a one-shot orchestrator instead of asking Claude/ChatGPT to chain the underlying tools manually.

name: pv.classify
description: Classify a planned study into its EMA pharmacovigilance regulatory category (PASS imposed/voluntary, PAES, RMP Annex 4, DUS, active surveillance registry, pregnancy registry, spontaneous reporting, ICH E2E plan). Returns the matching GVP module + ENCePP study-category label (not a registered protocol ID — consult the ENCePP Code of Conduct checklist for templates) + submission obligations + RMP implications + FDA analogue. Use BEFORE preparing an HTA dossier or before designing a post-authorisation study. Pass the structured `pv_classification` output to `hta_dossier` to populate its Pharmacovigilance Plan section. Enum values are case-insensitive — `"RCT"`/`"rct"`, `"EU"`/`"eu"` etc. all work.

name: jca.pico_scope
description: Produce the canonical EU Joint Clinical Assessment (JCA) PICO matrix for a drug-indication pair. Returns a consolidated PICO list (per JCA process under Reg. 2021/2282) plus country-specific comparator universes, outcome instrument preferences, population subgroup focus, and a heterogeneity warning. Pipe `pico_matrix.picos` directly into `hta_dossier({hta_body:"jca", picos: ...})`. v1 covers DE/FR/IT/ES/NL + UK (post-Brexit context). Heterogeneity warning fires at ≥3 distinct comparator molecules across ≥2 jurisdictions — a tool-level assumption, not a published EUnetHTA threshold; treat the warning as a prompt to run evidence_network + itc_feasibility, not as a definitive diagnosis. NSCLC EGFR-mutant comparator detail is currently modeled only for line_of_therapy="second_line"; other lines use a generic chemotherapy anchor with a warning. Enum values are case-insensitive — `"DE"`/`"de"`, `"first_line"`/`"First_Line"` etc. all work.

name: pv.signal_workflow
description: Compute disproportionality statistics (PRR, ROR, IC/BCPNN, MGPS/EBGM) on user-supplied drug-AE case counts and decide a signal verdict per EMA GVP Module IX rev 2. Returns the verdict (no/strengthening/confirmed/previously known/refuted), workflow recommendations, and canonical RMP signal-section text. To classify a finding as previously_known_signal, supply BOTH prior_known_signals AND reported_event so the tool can match the disproportionality to a specific known event. Optionally layers in GVP Considerations P.III pregnancy follow-up (birth/3mo/12mo) when both pregnancy_exposure and rmp_has_pregnancy_concern are true. Pairs with pv_classify. ⚠️ MGPS uses single-stratum gamma-Poisson shrinkage in v1 — when database counts are confounded by sex/age strata, EBGM/EB05 may be inflated; stratified MGPS is planned for v2. v1 takes user counts; v2 will also integrate EVDAS programmatic access per Reg. 2025/1466.

name: hta.workflow
description: End-to-end HTA submission orchestrator. One call runs literature_search (with PRISMA-style stability via runs=N) → screen_abstracts (PICO filter) → risk_of_bias (auto RoB 2/ROBINS-I/AMSTAR-2) → cost_effectiveness_model (Markov + 1k PSA, defaults from indication) → hta_dossier (auto-GRADE downgrade from RoB output) → validate_links (post-hoc URL audit). Returns a combined report with per-phase timings, the full dossier draft, and the URL validation table. Use as a single-shot drop-in replacement for the 4-5 separate prompts a generic LLM would need to chain these tools manually. Each phase wrapped in safe-run so single-step failures do not abort the pipeline.

name: irb.review
description: Classify a planned study under 45 CFR 46 (US Common Rule) + EU CTR 536/2014 to produce an IRB / Ethics Committee submission scaffold. Returns: review tier (exempt §46.104 cat 1-8 / expedited §46.110 cat 1-7 / full-board §46.108), EU CTR review path with timeline, vulnerable-population obligations (Subpart B/C/D), GDPR Art. 9 + HIPAA §164.514 data-management plan, SAE-reporting framework (CTR Annex III / FDA IND / PSUR), ICF complexity tier, COI framework (PHS 42 CFR 50 / EU CTR Art. 14), and a ready-to-paste cover letter. v1 covers EU+US; UK/Japan/Canada planned for v2. Optional pv_classification input ties IRB review to the regulatory PV category — when primary_category is PASS_imposed, SAE timelines override to CTR Annex III. Enum values are case-insensitive — `"interventional"`/`"Interventional"`, `"us_irb"`/`"US_IRB"` etc. all work.

name: icf.readability_check
description: Score the readability of an Informed Consent Form (ICF) text. Returns Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog Index, SMOG Grade, plus per-sentence breakdown identifying the worst offenders, medical-jargon detection with plain-language alternatives, and a pass/borderline/fail verdict vs a target grade level (default 8 per FDA / NIH guidance). Pairs with irb_review when planning a study — investigators paste the ICF draft, get back a concrete rewrite list. Pure logic, no external API.

name: evidence.clinical_scale
description: Score neurology & cognitive outcome scales (UMSARS/UPDRS/MDS-UPDRS/ADAS-Cog/MoCA/MMSE). Returns total + subscale scores, MCID-based responder classification, and trajectory comparison vs NNIPPS/PPMI/ADNI reference cohorts. Integrates with jca_pico_scope for MSA (neurology_msa, orphan Phase 2 2028)/PD (neurology_pd)/AD (neurology_ad) indication categories.

name: evidence.unmet_need
description: Generate a structured unmet need section for HTA dossiers (NICE STA, EMA, FDA, IQWiG, HAS, JCA, GVD, AMCP). Consume-only: first retrieve evidence with literature_search, then pass only cited facts across 4 HEOR dimensions — disease burden, treatment landscape, QoL impact, economic burden. By default (auto_check_regulatory=true), automatically checks current regulatory status of comparators in treatment_landscape.current_soc via primary-source databases (OpenFDA/EMA EPI) and injects verbatim label quotes with auto-numbered citations. Degrades gracefully on API errors — never blocks dossier output. Set auto_check_regulatory:false to skip. Produces a standardised markdown section plus a 1-paragraph unmet_need_summary for downstream tools. Pipe unmet_need_summary into hta_dossier(unmet_need_summary:...) to pre-fill NICE Section B (unmet need) or GVD Section 4. Design log #23 + #26.

name: regulatory.status_check
description: Look up current regulatory approval status for a drug from primary sources (OpenFDA for US, EMA EPI for EU). Returns approved indications, label text verbatim, age/weight/sex constraints, black-box warnings, REMS status, contraindications, source URLs, and fetch timestamp. Refuses to assert 'not approved' on database absence — emits 'unknown' instead. 24h cache with force_refresh flag. Use BEFORE any claim about approval status, pediatric indication, or regulatory restrictions. Design log #25.

name: hosting_importWordpressWebsite
description: Import a WordPress website from an archive file to a hosting server. This tool uploads a website archive (zip, tar, tar.gz, etc.) and a database dump (.sql file) to deploy a complete WordPress website. The archive will be extracted on the server automatically. Note: This process may take a while for larger sites. After upload completion, files are being extracted and the site will be available in a few minutes. The username will be automatically resolved from the domain.

name: hosting_deployWordpressPlugin
description: Deploy a WordPress plugin from a directory to a hosting server. This tool uploads all plugin files and triggers plugin deployment.

name: hosting_deployWordpressTheme
description: Deploy a WordPress theme from a directory to a hosting server. This tool uploads all theme files and triggers theme deployment. The uploaded theme can optionally be activated after deployment.

name: hosting_deployJsApplication
description: Deploy a JavaScript application from an archive file to a hosting server. IMPORTANT: the archive must ONLY contain application source files, not the build output, skip node_modules directory; also exclude all files matched by .gitignore if the ignore file exists. The build process will be triggered automatically on the server after the archive is uploaded. After deployment, use the hosting_listJsDeployments tool to check deployment status and track build progress.

name: hosting_deployStaticWebsite
description: Deploy a static website from an archive file to a hosting server. IMPORTANT: This tool only works for static websites with no build process. The archive must contain pre-built static files (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, etc.) ready to be served. If the website has a package.json file or requires a build command, use hosting_deployJsApplication instead. The archive will be extracted and deployed directly without any build steps. The username will be automatically resolved from the domain.

name: hosting_listJsDeployments
description: List javascript application deployments for checking their status. Use this tool when customer asks for the status of the deployment. This tool retrieves a paginated list of Node.js application deployments for a domain with optional filtering by deployment states.

name: hosting_showJsDeploymentLogs
description: Retrieve logs for a specified JavaScript application deployment for debugging purposes in case of failure.

name: billing_getCatalogItemListV1

Retrieve catalog items available for order.

Prices in catalog items is displayed as cents (without floating point),
e.g: float `17.99` is displayed as integer `1799`.

Use this endpoint to view available services and pricing before placing orders.

name: billing_setDefaultPaymentMethodV1

Set the default payment method for your account.

name: billing_deletePaymentMethodV1

description:
Retrieve available payment methods that can be used for placing new orders.

If you want to add new payment method,
please use [hPanel](https://hpanel.hostinger.com/billing/payment-methods).

Use this endpoint to view available payment options before creating orders.

name: billing_getSubscriptionListV1

Retrieve a list of all subscriptions associated with your account.

name: billing_disableAutoRenewalV1

name: billing_enableAutoRenewalV1

Enable auto-renewal for a subscription.

name: DNS_getDNSSnapshotV1
description:
Retrieve particular DNS snapshot with contents of DNS zone records.

Use this endpoint to view historical DNS configurations for domains.

name: DNS_getDNSSnapshotListV1
description:
Retrieve DNS snapshots for a domain.

name: DNS_restoreDNSSnapshotV1
description:
Restore DNS zone to the selected snapshot.

Use this endpoint to revert domain DNS to a previous configuration.

name: DNS_getDNSRecordsV1
description:
Retrieve DNS zone records for a specific domain.

Use this endpoint to view current DNS configuration for domain management.

name: DNS_updateDNSRecordsV1
description:
Update DNS records for the selected domain.

Using `overwrite = true` will replace existing records with the provided ones. 
Otherwise existing records will be updated and new records will be added.

Use this endpoint to modify domain DNS configuration.

name: DNS_deleteDNSRecordsV1
description:
Delete DNS records for the selected domain.

To filter which records to delete, add the `name` of the record and `type` to the filter. 
Multiple filters can be provided with single request.

If you have multiple records with the same name and type, and you want to delete only part of them,
refer to the `Update zone records` endpoint.

Use this endpoint to remove specific DNS records from domains.

name: DNS_resetDNSRecordsV1
description:
Reset DNS zone to the default records.

name: DNS_validateDNSRecordsV1
description:
Validate DNS records prior to update for the selected domain.

If the validation is successful, the response will contain `200 Success` code.
If there is validation error, the response will fail with `422 Validation error` code.

Use this endpoint to verify DNS record validity before applying changes.

name: v2_getDomainVerificationsDIRECT
description: Retrieve a list of pending and completed domain verifications.

name: domains_checkDomainAvailabilityV1
description:
Check availability of domain names across multiple TLDs.

Multiple TLDs can be checked at once.
If you want alternative domains with response, provide only one TLD and set `with_alternatives` to `true`.
TLDs should be provided without leading dot (e.g. `com`, `net`, `org`).

Endpoint has rate limit of 10 requests per minute.

Use this endpoint to verify domain availability before purchase.

name: domains_getDomainForwardingV1
description:
Retrieve domain forwarding data.

Use this endpoint to view current redirect configuration for domains.

name: domains_deleteDomainForwardingV1

Delete domain forwarding data.

name: domains_createDomainForwardingV1

Create domain forwarding configuration.

name: domains_enableDomainLockV1
description:
Enable domain lock for the domain.

When domain lock is enabled,
the domain cannot be transferred to another registrar without first disabling the lock.

name: domains_disableDomainLockV1
description:
Disable domain lock for the domain.

name: domains_getDomainDetailsV1
description:
Retrieve detailed information for specified domain.

name: domains_getDomainListV1

Retrieve all domains associated with your account.

Purchase and register a new domain name.

If registration fails, login to [hPanel](https://hpanel.hostinger.com/) and check domain registration status.

Use this endpoint to register new domains for users.

Enable privacy protection for the domain.

Set nameservers for a specified domain.
