- **Full reset**: Wipe everything (requires confirm_all=true)

⚠️ This permanently deletes ledger entries. Handoff state is preserved unless explicitly cleared.

name: session_compact_ledger
description:
Auto-compact old session ledger entries by rolling them up into AI-generated summaries. This prevents the ledger from growing indefinitely and keeps deep context loading fast.

How it works:
1. Finds projects with more entries than the threshold
2. Summarizes old entries using Gemini (keeps recent entries intact)
3. Inserts a rollup entry and archives the originals (soft-delete)

Use dry_run=true to preview what would be compacted without executing.

name: session_search_memory
description:
Search session history semantically (by meaning, not just keywords). Uses vector embeddings to find sessions with similar context, even when the exact wording differs. Requires pgvector extension in Supabase.

Complements knowledge_search (keyword-based) — use this when keyword search returns no results or when the query is phrased differently from stored summaries.

name: memory_history
description: View the timeline of past memory states for this project. Use this BEFORE memory_checkout to find the correct version to revert to. Shows version numbers, timestamps, and summaries of each saved state.

name: memory_checkout
description: Time travel! Restores the project's memory to a specific past version. This overwrites the current handoff state with the historical snapshot, like a Git revert — the version number moves forward (no data is lost). Call memory_history first to find the correct target_version.

name: session_save_image
description: Save a local image file into the project's permanent visual memory. Use this to remember UI states, diagrams, architecture graphs, or bug screenshots. The image is copied into Prism's media vault and indexed in the handoff metadata. On the next session_load_context, the agent will see a lightweight index of available images.

name: session_view_image
description: Retrieve an image from visual memory using its ID. Returns the image as Base64 inline content for the LLM to analyze. Use session_load_context first to see available image IDs.

name: session_health_check
description:
Run integrity checks on the agent's memory (like fsck for filesystems). Scans for missing embeddings, duplicate entries, orphaned handoffs, and stale rollups.

Checks performed:
1. **Missing embeddings** — entries that can't be found via semantic search
2. **Duplicate entries** — near-identical summaries wasting context tokens
3. **Orphaned handoffs** — handoff state with no backing ledger entries
4. **Stale rollups** — compaction artifacts with no archived originals

Use auto_fix=true to automatically repair missing embeddings and clean up orphans.

name: session_forget_memory
description:
Forget (delete) a specific memory entry by its ID. Supports two modes:

- **Soft delete** (default): Tombstones the entry — it stays in the database for audit trails but is excluded from all search results. Reversible.
- **Hard delete**: Permanently removes the entry from the database. Irreversible. Use only when GDPR Article 17 requires complete erasure.

⚠️ Soft delete is recommended for most use cases. The entry can be restored in the future if needed.

name: knowledge_set_retention
description:
Set an automatic data retention policy (TTL) for a project's memory. Entries older than ttl_days will be soft-deleted (archived) automatically on every server startup and every 12 hours while running.

**Use cases:**
- Set `ttl_days: 90` to auto-expire sessions older than 3 months
- Set `ttl_days: 0` to disable auto-expiry (default)

**Note:** Rollup/compaction entries are never expired — only raw sessions.

name: session_save_experience
description:
Record a typed experience event. Unlike session_save_ledger (flat logs), this captures structured behavioral data for pattern detection.

Event Types:
- **correction**: Agent was corrected by user
- **success**: Task completed successfully
- **failure**: Task failed
- **learning**: New knowledge acquired
- **validation_result**: Verification sandbox passed or failed

name: knowledge_upvote
description: Upvote a memory entry to increase its importance (graduation). Entries with importance >= 7 become 'graduated' insights that always surface in behavioral warnings.

name: knowledge_downvote
description: Downvote a memory entry to decrease its importance. Importance cannot go below 0.

name: knowledge_sync_rules
description:
Auto-sync graduated insights (importance >= 7) into your project's IDE rules file (.cursorrules or .clauderules). This bridges behavioral memory with static IDE context — turning dynamic agent learnings into always-on rules.

**How it works:**
1. Fetches graduated insights from the ledger
2. Formats them as markdown rules inside sentinel markers
3. Idempotently writes them into the target file at the project's configured repo_path

**Requirements:** The project must have a repo_path configured in the dashboard.

**Idempotency:** Uses `<!-- PRISM:AUTO-RULES:START -->` / `<!-- PRISM:AUTO-RULES:END -->` sentinel markers. Running this tool multiple times produces the same file. User-maintained content outside the sentinels is never touched.

name: deep_storage_purge
description:
v5.1 Deep Storage Mode: Purge high-precision float32 embedding vectors for entries that already have TurboQuant compressed blobs, reclaiming ~90% of vector storage. Only affects entries older than the specified threshold (default: 30 days, minimum: 7). Entries without compressed blobs are NEVER touched. Use dry_run=true to preview the impact before executing.

**When to use:** After running TurboQuant backfill (session_backfill_embeddings), call this tool to reclaim disk space from legacy float32 vectors that are no longer needed for search.

**Safety:** Tier-2 search (TurboQuant) maintains 95%+ accuracy with compressed blobs. Tier-3 (FTS5 keyword) search is completely unaffected.

name: session_export_memory
description:
Export all of a project's memory to a local file. Fulfills GDPR Article 20 (Right to Data Portability) and the 'local-first' portability promise.

**What is exported:**
- All session ledger entries (summaries, decisions, TODOs, file changes)
- Current handoff state (live project context)
- System settings (API keys are "**REDACTED**" for security)
- Visual memory index (descriptions, captions, timestamps; not the raw files)

**Formats:**
- `json` — machine-readable, suitable for import into another Prism instance
- `markdown` — human-readable, ideal for static archiving
- `vault` — Prism-Port: exports a compressed `.zip` of interrelated Markdown files with proper Obsidian/Logseq YAML frontmatter and `[[Wikilinks]]`

⚠️ Output directory must exist and be writable. Filenames are auto-generated: `prism-export-<project>-<date>.(json|md|zip)`

name: session_backfill_links
description:
Retroactively create graph edges (memory links) for all existing entries in a project. This builds the associative memory graph from your existing session history.

Three strategies are run:
1. **Temporal Chaining**: Links consecutive entries within the same conversation
2. **Keyword Overlap**: Links entries sharing ≥3 keywords (bidirectional)
3. **Provenance**: Links rollup summaries to their archived originals

All strategies use INSERT OR IGNORE — safe to re-run multiple times.

**When to use:** Run once after upgrading to v6.0 to populate the graph for existing memories. New entries are auto-linked on save (no manual action needed).

name: session_synthesize_edges
description:
Step 3A Edge Synthesis: Scans recent project entries with embeddings, finds high-similarity but currently disconnected entries, and creates inferred links as 'synthesized_from'.

**On-Demand Graph Enrichment**: Use this tool periodically to discover semantic relationships between structurally disconnected memory nodes. It batch processes the newest active entries.

name: session_cognitive_route
description: Resolve an HDC compositional state into a nearest semantic concept with policy-gated routing. Returns concept, confidence, distance, ambiguity, convergence steps, and route outcome. Use this for explainable cognitive recall decisions in v6.5.

name: maintenance_vacuum
description:
Reclaim disk space after large purge operations by running VACUUM on the local SQLite database.

Best called after `deep_storage_purge` removes many entries — SQLite reclaims page allocations only when explicitly vacuumed, so the file size stays the same until you call this tool.

For remote (Supabase) backends, returns guidance on triggering maintenance via the dashboard.

**Note:** On large databases this may take up to 60 seconds. The tool runs synchronously so you will know when it is safe to proceed.

name: onboarding_wizard
description:
Interactive setup wizard for new Prism users. Provides a step-by-step guided experience to get productive in under 3 minutes.

**Actions:**
- `start` — Begin the wizard from step 1
- `next` — Advance to the next step
- `status` — Check current wizard progress
- `skip` — Skip to completion

Each step returns instructions, code snippets, and progress percentage.

name: extract_entities
description:
Extract named entities from raw text using rule-based + optional LLM extraction. Automatically identifies technologies, file paths, decisions, TODOs, people, projects, and configuration values without explicit tagging.

**Entity types:** PERSON, PROJECT, TECH, FILE, DECISION, TODO, CONFIG

Use this to auto-enrich session context with structured metadata from raw conversation text.

name: api_analytics
description:
View API usage analytics per project or system-wide. Shows call counts, success rates, latency, token usage, top tools, and daily trends.

**Scopes:**
- `project` — Analytics for a specific project
- `system` — System-wide aggregate analytics

name: backup_database
description:
Create, list, or restore SQLite database backups.

**Actions:**
- `create` — Create a new backup now
- `list` — List available backups with sizes and ages
- `restore` — Restore from a specific backup file
- `configure` — Set backup schedule (hourly/daily/weekly)

Backups are stored in ~/.prism/backups/ by default. Automatic retention pruning keeps only the configured maximum.

name: configure_notifications
description:
Configure real-time notifications for memory events via webhook, Slack, or email.

**Actions:**
- `status` — Show current notification configuration
- `add_channel` — Add a notification channel (webhook/slack/email)
- `remove_channel` — Remove a channel by URL
- `test` — Send a test notification to all configured channels

**Events:** health_degradation, compaction_complete, backup_complete, backup_failed, memory_threshold, new_graduated_insight, scheduler_error

name: query_memory_natural
description:
Query memories using natural language instead of structured tool syntax. Automatically classifies intent, extracts keywords, and executes the appropriate search strategy.

**Examples:**
- "What did we decide about authentication?"
- "What's still open on the billing project?"
- "What files did we change last week?"
- "Show me recent work on the API"

Returns the parsed intent, search results, and optionally an LLM-synthesized answer.

name: provision_postgres_project
description: Provision a new Postgres database. Returns project credentials on success, or payment details if x402 payment is needed.

name: run_sql
description: Execute SQL (DDL or queries) against a provisioned project. Returns results as a markdown table.

name: rest_query
description: Query or mutate data via the PostgREST REST API. Supports GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE with query params.

name: apply_expose
description: Apply a declarative authorization manifest to a project (POST /projects/v1/admin/:id/expose). The manifest describes the full authorization surface: tables (with policy, owner_column, force_owner_on_insert, i_understand_this_is_unrestricted, custom_sql), views (with base, select, filter), and rpcs (with signature, grant_to). Convergent: applying the same manifest twice is a no-op; items dropped between applies have their policies/grants/triggers/views revoked. Tables are dark by default — any table not declared with expose:true is unreachable via anon/authenticated.

name: validate_manifest
description: Validate an auth/expose manifest without applying it. This checks the authorization manifest used by manifest.json, database.expose, and apply_expose; it is not deploy-manifest validation. Optional migration_sql is reference context only and is not executed. Use deploy planning/dry-run surfaces for deploy manifest questions.

name: get_expose
description: Get the current authorization manifest for a project (GET /projects/v1/admin/:id/expose). Returns the last-applied manifest from `internal.project_manifest`, or a manifest reconstructed by introspecting live DB state if none has ever been applied. The `source` field is `"applied"` or `"introspected"`.

name: get_schema
description: Introspect the database schema — tables, columns, types, constraints, and RLS policies. Useful for understanding the database structure before writing queries.

name: get_usage
description: Get project usage report — API calls, storage usage, limits, and lease expiry.

name: assets_put
description: Upload a blob (file or inline content) to project storage via direct-to-S3. Accepts local_path (any size up to 5 TiB) or content (≤ 1 MB inline). Public blobs get a CDN URL; private blobs require authenticated reads. Use `immutable: true` to produce a content-addressed URL that never needs cache invalidation.

name: assets_get
description: Download a blob to a local file path. Writes bytes directly to disk (no context-window bloat). Returns size + SHA-256 header (if the blob has one stored).

name: assets_ls
description: List blobs in a project with optional prefix filter over a flat key namespace. Supports pagination via cursor.

name: assets_rm
description: Delete a blob from project storage and decrement the project's storage_bytes.

name: assets_sign
description: Generate a time-boxed S3 presigned GET URL for a blob. Use this to share a private blob externally without exposing your apikey. Default TTL 1 hour, max 7 days.

name: diagnose_public_url
description: Returns the live CDN state for a public blob URL (probed once from gateway-us-east-1 — NOT a global view). Use this when a deployed asset shows the wrong version or you suspect cache staleness. The result includes `expectedSha256` (from gateway DB), `observedSha256` (what CloudFront just served), recent `invalidation` status, and a human-readable `hint` with actionable next-steps. The `probeMayHaveWarmedCache: true` field warns that the probe itself populates the cache, so subsequent reads from elsewhere may differ. URLs outside the requesting project return 403; non-`*.run402.com` URLs return 400 unless they're on one of your active custom domains.

name: wait_for_cdn_freshness
description: Polls the CDN until a MUTABLE blob URL serves the expected SHA-256, or the timeout elapses. **For mutable URLs only** — for immutable URLs (the `immutableUrl` returned by `assets_put`), no waiting is needed; they're bound to a SHA at upload time and never previously cached. Use this after a re-upload to an existing public mutable key when an end-user-visible URL must reflect the new content before continuing. The probe is single-vantage (us-east-1). On timeout, the tool returns isError=true so an agent can branch into a fallback — typically: switch to the immutableUrl.

name: deploy_function
description: Deploy a serverless function (Node 22) to a project. Handler signature: export default async (req: Request) => Response. The function can `import { db, adminDb, getUser, email, ai } from '@run402/functions'` — auto-bundled by the platform. Additional npm packages are bundled at deploy time when listed in `deps` (bare names resolve to latest; pinned/range specs are honored verbatim; `@run402/functions` and `run402-functions` rejected; max 30 entries; native binaries rejected). The response includes `runtime_version` (the bundled `@run402/functions` version — surface as 'Functions runtime version', never bare 'runtime'), `deps_resolved` (map of dep name → installed concrete version), and an optional top-level `warnings` array (sibling to the function record).

name: invoke_function
description: Invoke a deployed function via HTTP. Returns the function's response body and status code. Useful for testing functions without building a frontend.

name: get_function_logs
description: Get recent logs from a deployed function. Shows console.log/error output and error stack traces from CloudWatch.

name: list_functions
description: List all deployed functions for a project. Shows names, URLs, runtime, timeout, memory, and (for functions deployed under bundling-at-deploy) the Functions runtime version (`@run402/functions` version) and resolved direct deps. Functions deployed before that change have `runtime_version` and `deps_resolved` set to null.

name: delete_function
description: Delete a deployed function from a project.

name: update_function
description: Update a function's schedule, timeout, or memory without re-deploying code. Pass schedule as a cron expression to set/update, or null to remove.

name: set_secret
description: Set a project secret (e.g. STRIPE_SECRET_KEY). Values are write-only and injected as process.env variables in functions. Setting an existing key overwrites it. Use this before deploy, then declare the key with secrets.require.

name: list_secrets
description: List secret keys for a project. Values and value-derived hashes are never shown; use this only to check which keys are configured.

name: delete_secret
description: Delete a secret from a project.

name: jobs_submit
description: Submit a fixed platform-managed job. The request must match the gateway jobs API shape: job_type, input with input.json, and max_cost_usd_micros. The SDK supplies the required idempotency header.

name: jobs_get
description: Get a managed job run by id.

name: jobs_logs
description: Read recent runner logs for a managed job. Use tail to cap entries and since for an epoch millisecond lower bound.

name: jobs_cancel
description: Cancel a queued or running managed job.

name: deploy_site
description: Deploy a static site (HTML/CSS/JS) from inline file bytes. Files are staged to a temp directory, then uploaded via the v1.32 plan/commit transport — only bytes the gateway doesn't already have are PUT. Served at a unique URL via CloudFront. Free with active tier.

name: deploy_site_dir
description: Deploy a static site from a local directory. Walks the tree, hashes each file, and uploads only the bytes the gateway doesn't already have via the v1.32 plan/commit transport. Files named .git, node_modules, or .DS_Store are skipped; symlinks are rejected. Re-deploying an unchanged tree issues no S3 PUTs. Free with active tier.

name: deploy
description: Unified deploy primitive (v1.34+). Accepts a structured ReleaseSpec — database (migrations + expose), value-free secrets.require/delete declarations, functions, site, site.public_paths, subdomains, and routes.replace web routes — with explicit replace vs patch semantics per resource. Use site.public_paths for clean static URLs such as /events backed by release asset events.html; explicit mode does not expose /events.html unless separately declared, while mode: 'implicit' restores filename-derived reachability and can widen access. Route entries map exact/final-wildcard browser paths like /admin and /admin/* to Node 22 Fetch Request -> Response functions, or exact GET/HEAD method-aware static aliases such as /events to { type: 'static', file: 'events.html' }; intentional read-only GET/HEAD wildcard function routes may set acknowledge_readonly: true. Direct /functions/v1/:name remains API-key protected. Secret values must be set first with set_secret, never placed in deploy specs. All bytes ride through CAS (no inline-body cap). Returns release_id, URLs, warnings, and a structured progress-event log. Stops before upload/commit on confirmation-required warnings unless reviewed codes are passed with allow_warning_codes or allow_warnings is true.

name: deploy_diagnose_url
description: Read-only authenticated diagnostics for a Run402 public URL or host/path pair. Explains whether the current live release would serve the URL, including match, diagnostic body status, static manifest/cache metadata when returned, structured warnings for ignored query/fragment, and next steps. This does not fetch bytes, purge cache, mutate deploy state, or expose internal CAS URLs.

name: deploy_resume
description: Resume a deploy operation that ended in `activation_pending` or `schema_settling` (e.g. transient gateway failure between SQL commit and the pointer-swap activation). The gateway re-runs only the failed phase forward — SQL is never replayed. Idempotent: calling on an already-terminal operation returns the snapshot without re-running.

name: deploy_list
description: List recent deploy operations for a project. Returns operation_id, status, release_id, and timestamps. Use this to build deploy-history UIs or to find a recent operation_id to feed into `deploy_resume` / `deploy_events`. Pass `limit` to bound the result set; the gateway also returns a `cursor` for pagination when there are more.

name: deploy_events
description: Fetch the recorded phase-event stream for a deploy operation. Returns the same `DeployEvent` shapes the `deploy` tool emits inline during an in-flight deploy — useful for inspecting a deploy after the fact (e.g., a deploy that the agent didn't observe directly, or one being resumed from a different process).

name: deploy_release_get
description: Fetch a release inventory by id. Returns release metadata, effective/desired state kind, site path inventory, function inventory, secret keys, subdomains, and applied migrations. Use `site_limit` to cap large site inventories. Canonical SDK errors are preserved.

name: deploy_release_active
description: Fetch the current-live release inventory for a project. Returns `release_id: null` with an empty current-live inventory when no release is active yet. Use this before deploy diffs to understand what is currently serving. Canonical SDK errors are preserved.

name: deploy_release_diff
description: Diff two release targets for a project. `from` may be `empty`, `active`, or a release id; `to` may be `active` or a release id. Returns release-to-release diff buckets and `migrations.applied_between_releases`. Semantic gateway errors such as invalid targets, same-release diffs, or no active release are preserved.

name: ci_create_binding
description: Create a GitHub Actions CI/OIDC deploy binding by sending a locally signed delegation to the SDK. This MCP wrapper does not sign or broaden authority; the signed delegation defines the repository/branch or environment, allowed events/actions, and optional route_scopes. Without route_scopes, CI cannot deploy route declarations.

name: ci_list_bindings
description: List CI/OIDC deploy bindings for a project, including route_scopes when delegated. Use this to inspect which GitHub Actions subjects can deploy before editing bindings.

name: ci_get_binding
description: Get one CI/OIDC deploy binding by id, including its subject, allowed events/actions, repository id, revocation state, and route_scopes.

name: ci_revoke_binding
description: Revoke one CI/OIDC deploy binding. Revocation stops future CI gateway requests, but does not undo already deployed releases or rotate secrets.

name: claim_subdomain
description: Claim a custom subdomain (e.g. myapp.run402.com) and point it at an existing deployment. Free, requires service_key auth.

name: delete_subdomain
description: Release a custom subdomain. The URL will stop serving content.

name: list_subdomains
description: List all subdomains claimed by a project.

name: add_custom_domain
description: Register a custom domain (e.g. example.com) to point at a Run402 subdomain. Returns DNS instructions for the human to configure.

name: list_custom_domains
description: List all custom domains registered for a project.

name: check_domain_status
description: Check if a custom domain's DNS is configured and SSL is active. Poll this after registering a domain.

name: remove_custom_domain
description: Release a custom domain mapping. Traffic to the domain will no longer route to Run402.

name: browse_apps
description: Browse public apps available for forking. Optionally filter by tags.

name: fork_app
description: Fork a published app into a new project. Creates a full copy including database, functions, site, and optionally claims a subdomain.

name: publish_app
description: Publish a project as a forkable app. Set visibility and tags for discoverability.

name: list_versions
description: List published versions of a project.

name: get_quote
description: Get tier pricing for Run402 projects. Free, no auth required. Shows prices, lease durations, storage limits, and API call limits.

name: tier_status
description: Check current tier subscription — tier name, status, expiry, usage, and function authoring caps when returned (max timeout, memory, scheduled functions, min cron interval). Requires allowance auth.

name: set_tier
description: Subscribe, renew, or upgrade tier. Auto-detects action based on allowance state. Returns success or payment details if x402 payment is needed.

name: delete_project
description: Immediately and irreversibly delete a project: the gateway runs the full destructive cascade (drop tenant schema, delete Lambda functions, release subdomains, tombstone mailbox, remove sender domain, wipe secrets and app versions) and sets status=purged. This tool also removes the project from the local key store. Distinct from the automatic lease-expiry grace window — this action is the explicit purge and cannot be undone. To recover from a missed renewal use `set_tier` instead.

name: pin_project
description: Pin a project so it is not garbage-collected or expired. Admin only — uses the configured allowance wallet for run402 platform admin auth; project owners authenticating with service_key or a non-admin SIWX wallet will receive 403 admin_required. Not a self-service command for regular users.

name: promote_user
description: Promote a user to project_admin role by email. Admins can manage secrets from the browser. Requires service_key.

name: demote_user
description: Demote a user from project_admin role by email. Reverts to default authenticated role. Requires service_key.

name: check_balance
description: Check billing account balance for an agent allowance address. Shows available and held funds.

name: list_projects
description: List all active projects for an agent allowance address.

name: allowance_status
description: Check local agent allowance status — address, network, and funding status.

name: allowance_create
description: Create a new local agent allowance (Base Sepolia testnet). Generates a private key and derives the Ethereum address. Saved to ~/.config/run402/allowance.json.

name: allowance_export
description: Export the local agent allowance address. Safe to share publicly.

name: request_faucet
description: Request free testnet USDC from the Run402 faucet (Base Sepolia). Rate limit: 1 per IP per 24h. Returns 0.25 USDC — enough for 2 prototype databases.

name: generate_image
description: Generate a PNG image from a text prompt. Costs $0.03 USDC via x402. Aspect ratios: square (1:1), landscape (16:9), portrait (9:16).

name: create_mailbox
description: Create a project-scoped email mailbox at <slug>@mail.run402.com. One mailbox per project.

name: send_email
description: Send an email from the project's mailbox. Two modes: template (project_invite, magic_link, notification) or raw HTML (subject + html). Optional from_name for display name. Single recipient only.

name: list_emails
description: List sent emails from the project's mailbox. Shows message ID, template, recipient, status, and timestamp.

name: get_email
description: Get a sent email with details and any replies.

name: get_email_raw
description: Get the raw RFC-822 bytes of an inbound email message, base64-encoded. The decoded bytes are bit-identical to the DKIM-signed original — no parsing, normalization, or CRLF cleanup. Use this for cryptographic verification (DKIM checks, zk-email proofs). Inbound messages only; outbound returns 404. For display/threading, use get_email instead.

name: get_mailbox
description: Get the project's mailbox info (ID, address, slug). Use to check if a mailbox exists.

name: delete_mailbox
description: Delete the project's mailbox (irreversible — drops all messages and webhook subscriptions). Requires confirm=true. If mailbox_id is omitted, resolves the project's mailbox.

name: register_mailbox_webhook
description: Register a webhook on the project's mailbox. Receives POST notifications for email events (delivery, bounced, complained, reply_received).

name: list_mailbox_webhooks
description: List all webhooks registered on the project's mailbox.

name: get_mailbox_webhook
description: Get details of a specific webhook by ID.

name: delete_mailbox_webhook
description: Delete a webhook. Idempotent — succeeds even if already deleted.

name: update_mailbox_webhook
description: Update a webhook's URL and/or events. At least one field required. Events is a full replacement, not a merge.

name: ai_translate
description: Translate text to a target language. Requires service key and active AI Translation add-on. Supports optional source language and context hint.

name: ai_moderate
description: Run content moderation on text. Returns flagged status and category scores. Free for all projects, requires service key.

name: ai_usage
description: Get AI translation usage for the current billing period — used words, quota, and remaining balance.

name: send_message
description: Send a message to the Run402 developers. Requires an active tier.

name: set_agent_contact
description: Register agent contact info (name, email, webhook). New or changed emails start operator email reply verification. Free with allowance auth.

name: get_agent_contact_status
description: Get the current agent contact assurance state: wallet_only, email_pending, email_verified, passkey_pending, or operator_passkey.

name: verify_agent_contact_email
description: Start or resend the operator email reply challenge for the active agent contact email. Does not expose the challenge secret.

name: start_operator_passkey_enrollment
description: Email a short-lived Run402 operator passkey enrollment link to the verified contact email. Requires email_verified.

name: create_checkout
description: Create a Stripe checkout URL for your human to fund your agent allowance with a credit card.

name: billing_history
description: View billing transaction history for an agent allowance address.

name: update_version
description: Update metadata (description, tags, visibility, fork_allowed) of a published app version.

name: delete_version
description: Delete a published app version.

name: get_app
description: Inspect a specific published app — details, required secrets, fork pricing.

name: init
description: Set up agent allowance, request faucet funding, and check tier status — single-call bootstrap. Idempotent, safe to re-run.

name: status
description: Full account snapshot — allowance, billing balance, tier subscription, projects, and active project. Single-call overview.

name: project_info
description: Show local project details — REST URL, keys, site URL, and deployment info. Reads from local keystore only.

name: project_use
description: Set the active/default project in the local keystore.

name: project_keys
description: Get anon_key and service_key for a project from the local keystore.

name: request_magic_link
description: Send a passwordless login email (magic link) to a project user. Auto-creates the user on first verification. Rate limited per email (5/hr) and per project (by tier).

name: verify_magic_link
description: Exchange a magic link token for access_token + refresh_token. Creates the user if they don't exist. Token is single-use and expires in 15 minutes.

name: create_auth_user
description: Create or update a project auth user with the service key. Can set project_admin and optionally send a trusted invite.

name: invite_auth_user
description: Create/update a project auth user and send a trusted invite magic link. Requires service_key and an allowed redirect_url.

name: set_user_password
description: Change, reset, or set a user's password. Change: provide current_password + new_password. Reset (via magic link login): just new_password. Set (passwordless user): requires allow_password_set=true on project.

name: auth_settings
description: Update project auth settings: allow_password_set, preferred_sign_in_method, public_signup, and require_passkey_for_project_admin. Requires service_key.

name: passkey_register_options
description: Create WebAuthn passkey registration options for the authenticated user.

name: passkey_register_verify
description: Verify a browser WebAuthn registration response and store the user's passkey.

name: passkey_login_options
description: Create WebAuthn passkey login options for a project app origin.

name: passkey_login_verify
description: Verify a browser WebAuthn assertion and return a normal Run402 auth session.

name: list_passkeys
description: List the authenticated user's active passkeys.

name: delete_passkey
description: Delete one authenticated-user passkey by id.

name: register_sender_domain
description: Register a custom email sending domain for a project. Returns DNS records (DKIM CNAMEs + SPF/DMARC) to add. Once verified, email sends from your domain instead of mail.run402.com.

name: sender_domain_status
description: Check the verification status of a project's custom sender domain. Polls SES for pending domains.

name: remove_sender_domain
description: Remove a project's custom sender domain. Email reverts to sending from mail.run402.com.

name: enable_sender_domain_inbound
description: Enable inbound email on a verified custom sender domain. Replies to <slug>@<your-domain> will route through run402. Requires DKIM-verified domain. Returns the MX record to add to DNS.

name: disable_sender_domain_inbound
description: Disable inbound email on a custom sender domain. Replies to <slug>@<your-domain> will no longer be delivered.

name: create_email_billing_account
description: Create an email-based billing account (Stripe-only, no wallet required). Sends a verification email. Idempotent — duplicate emails return the existing account.

name: link_wallet_to_account
description: Link a wallet to an existing email billing account, enabling hybrid Stripe + x402 access. Fails if the wallet is already linked elsewhere.

name: tier_checkout
description: Subscribe/renew/upgrade to a run402 tier via Stripe credit card. Alternative to x402 on-chain payment. Supports wallet or email identifier. Returns a Stripe checkout URL.

name: buy_email_pack
description: Buy a $5 email pack (10,000 emails, never expire). Pack credits activate when tier daily limit is exhausted AND a custom sender domain is verified. Returns a Stripe checkout URL.

name: set_auto_recharge
description: Enable or disable automatic email pack repurchase when credits drop below a threshold. Requires a saved Stripe payment method.

name: provision_contract_wallet
description: Provision an AWS KMS-backed Ethereum wallet for signing smart-contract write transactions. Private keys never leave KMS. Cost: $0.04/day rental ($1.20/month) plus $0.000005 per contract call. Requires $1.20 in cash credit at creation (30 days of rent). Non-custodial.

name: get_contract_wallet
description: Get a KMS contract wallet's metadata + live native-token balance + USD-micros (Chainlink-cached price).

name: list_contract_wallets
description: List all KMS contract wallets owned by the project, including deleted ones.

name: set_recovery_address
description: Set or clear the optional recovery address used for auto-drain on day-90 deletion of a KMS contract wallet.

name: set_low_balance_alert
description: Set the low-balance threshold (in wei) for a KMS contract wallet. Email alerts fire when the wallet's native balance drops below this threshold.

name: contract_call
description: Submit a smart-contract write call from a KMS wallet. The gateway encodes via viem, signs the digest via AWS KMS, and broadcasts. Idempotent on optional idempotency_key. Cost: chain gas at-cost + $0.000005 KMS sign fee per call.

name: contract_read
description: Read-only smart-contract call (view/pure functions). No signing, no gas, no billing — pure RPC convenience.

name: get_contract_call_status
description: Look up a previously submitted contract call by call_id. Returns lifecycle state (pending/confirmed/failed), block number, gas used, gas cost in USD-micros, receipt, and any error.

name: drain_contract_wallet
description: Drain a KMS contract wallet's entire native-token balance to a destination address. Works on suspended wallets — the safety valve. Cost: chain gas + $0.000005 KMS sign fee.

name: delete_contract_wallet
description: Schedule the KMS key for a contract wallet for deletion (7-day AWS minimum window). Refused if the wallet has on-chain balance ≥ dust — drain first.

name: service_status
description: Reports on the Run402 SERVICE (availability, capabilities, operator, deployment) — not your account. For your account status (allowance, tier, projects), use `status`. Reads public GET /status. No auth, no allowance required.

name: service_health
description: Liveness check for the Run402 SERVICE — not your account. For your account status (allowance, tier, projects), use `status`. Reads public GET /health with per-dependency check results. No auth required.

name: search_stations
description: Search for Swiss train stations, addresses, or points of interest by name. Returns UIC station IDs (e.g. "8503000" for Zürich HB) used by the other tools. Note: search_connections accepts station names directly, so this tool is only needed when the user explicitly asks for station info or when you need disambiguation between multiple matches.

name: search_connections
description: Find train connections between two Swiss stations. Accepts station names directly (e.g. "Zürich HB", "Bern") or UIC IDs — name resolution happens internally. Returns live schedules with departure/arrival times, duration, transfers, and trip IDs for downstream pricing/details/ticket calls. Live data: includes delays and cancellations for trains departing within 30 min.

name: get_trip_details
description: Get detailed information about a specific train connection including all intermediate stops, platforms, and occupancy. Use a trip ID from search_connections results.

name: get_more_connections
description: Load earlier or later train connections for a previous search. Use the collection ID from search_connections results.

name: get_prices
description: Get ticket prices in CHF for one or more train connections. Supports Half-Fare card (Halbtax) and GA travelcard discounts. Up to 10 trip_ids per call — batch them in a single request rather than calling once per connection. Use trip_ids from a recent search_connections result; do not invent IDs.

name: get_ticket_link
description: Get a direct purchase link to buy a train ticket on SBB.ch. Only call this when the user wants to buy a specific ticket. On mobile with SBB app installed, opens directly in the app with Halbtax/GA applied automatically.

name: search-content
description: Search screen text, audio transcriptions, input events, and memories. Returns timestamped results with app context. IMPORTANT: prefer activity-summary for broad questions ('what was I doing?'). Use search-content only when you need specific text/content. Start with limit=5, increase only if needed. Results can be large — use max_content_length=500 to truncate.

name: list-meetings
description: List detected meetings (Zoom, Teams, Meet, etc.) with duration, app, and attendees. Only available when screenpipe runs in smart transcription mode.

name: activity-summary
description: Rich activity overview: app usage, window/tab titles with URLs and time spent, key text per context, audio transcriptions. USE THIS FIRST for broad questions: 'what was I doing?', 'how long on X?', 'which apps?'. The 'windows' field shows exactly what the user worked on (e.g. 'Debug crash issue — 20 min', 'Stripe pricing page — 5 min'). Usually sufficient without further searches.

name: search-elements
description: Search UI elements (buttons, links, text fields) from the accessibility tree. Lighter than search-content for targeted UI lookups. Use when you need to find specific UI controls or page structure, not general content.

name: frame-context
description: Get full accessibility text, parsed tree nodes, and URLs for a specific frame ID. Use after search-content to get detailed context for a specific moment.

name: export-video
description: Export an MP4 video of screen recordings for a time range. Returns the file path. Can take a few minutes for long ranges.

name: update-memory
description: Create, update, or delete a persistent memory (facts, preferences, decisions the user wants to remember). To retrieve memories, use search-content with content_type='memory'. To create: provide content + tags. To update: provide id + fields to change. To delete: provide id + delete=true.

name: send-notification
description: Send a notification to the screenpipe desktop UI. Use to alert the user about findings, completed tasks, or actions needing attention.

name: health-check
description: Check if screenpipe is running and healthy. Returns recording status, frame/audio stats, timestamps.

name: list-audio-devices
description: List available audio input/output devices for recording.

name: list-monitors
description: List available monitors/screens for capture.

name: add-tags
description: Add tags to a content item (vision frame or audio chunk) for organization and retrieval.

name: search-speakers
description: Search for speakers by name prefix. Returns speaker ID, name, and metadata.

name: list-unnamed-speakers
description: List speakers that haven't been named yet. Useful for speaker identification workflow.

name: update-speaker
description: Rename a speaker or update their metadata.

name: merge-speakers
description: Merge two speakers into one (e.g. when the same person was detected as different speakers).

name: start-meeting
description: Manually start a meeting recording session.

name: stop-meeting
description: Stop the current manual meeting recording session.

name: get-meeting
description: Get details of a specific meeting by ID, including transcription and attendees.

name: update-meeting
description: Update a meeting's mutable fields (title, attendees, note, app, start/end). Partial: only the fields you pass are written, others stay as-is. Use this to save an AI-generated summary into the meeting note — read the current note first via get-meeting and pass the existing notes plus your additions so you don't overwrite the user's writing. Convention: append AI-generated summary text under a `## Summary` heading at the bottom of the existing note.

name: keyword-search
description: Fast keyword search using FTS index. Faster than search-content for exact keyword matching. Returns frame IDs and matched text.

name: get-frame-elements
description: Get all UI elements for a specific frame. More targeted than search-elements when you already have a frame_id.

name: control-recording
description: Start or stop audio/screen recording. Use to pause/resume capture.

name: list_shadcn_components
description: Get a list of all available shadcn/ui components

name: get_component_details
description: Get detailed information about a specific shadcn/ui component

name: get_component_examples
description: Get usage examples for a specific shadcn/ui component

name: search_components
description: Search for shadcn/ui components by keyword

name: spartanode_create_project
description: Create a new project in SpartaNode. Returns the project slug which you'll need for subsequent tool calls (list_tasks, sync_gantt, etc.).

name: spartanode_list_projects
description: List all SpartaNode projects the user has access to

name: spartanode_list_tasks
description: List all tasks in a project's development roadmap (Gantt chart) with their status, steps, and position

name: spartanode_get_task
description: Get full context for a specific task: prompt, plan (PLAN.md), steps, branch, status. Use this before working on a task locally.

name: spartanode_get_gantt_context
description: Get the full development roadmap context (GANTT_CONTEXT.md) showing all tasks and their status. Useful for understanding what other tasks exist before planning.

name: spartanode_export_gantt
description:
Export the current Gantt chart as a GANTT.md file. This is the source of truth for the project roadmap. You can edit this markdown, then re-sync it with spartanode_sync_gantt to update the chart.

External IDs (G-xxx) track task identity across edits — don't remove them. Add new tasks without an ID and they'll get one on sync.

name: spartanode_import_gantt
description: Import a GANTT.md file from the current working directory (or a specified path) into a project's roadmap. Parses the markdown format with G-xxx external IDs, phases, tags, steps, and syncs to the control plane. Use this after editing GANTT.md locally.

name: spartanode_update_task_status
description: Update the status of a task or a specific step within a task. Use after completing work locally.

name: spartanode_start_task
description: Start working on a task locally: fetches the latest branch, checks it out, writes PLAN.md and GANTT_CONTEXT.md to the repo root, and shows the current step to work on. Run this from the project's git repo directory.

name: spartanode_complete_step
description: Complete the current step: stages all changes, commits with a descriptive message, pushes the branch, marks the step as done in the Gantt, and shows the next step. Run from the project's git repo directory.

name: spartanode_sync_gantt
description:
Generate or update a project's Gantt chart from a structured development plan. Use this when you've discussed a project plan with the user and want to materialize it as tasks in the roadmap.

If the project doesn't exist yet, it will be auto-created. Provide gitUrl and defaultBranch if you want to link a repo.

**Diff-aware sync:** Tasks with external IDs (G-xxx from GANTT.md) are matched against existing tasks:
- New tasks (no matching ID) → created
- Existing idea/planned tasks → updated (replaced)
- Running/done/merged tasks → PROTECTED, never touched. Conflicts reported.
- Tasks removed from the plan but still in idea/planned → deleted
- Tasks removed but running/done → kept, reported as protected

Set clearExisting=true to replace ALL idea/planned tasks (ignores external ID matching).

Tags: frontend, backend, infra, bugfix, design, docs, test, data, trading, risk, research, executive, reporting, execution, compliance (or any custom tag).
Column values determine execution order: same column = parallel, sequential = in order.
Span = bar width in columns (default 1).

name: spartanode_spawn_task
description: Trigger the automated container pipeline for a task (same as clicking 'Run Gantt' in the browser). The task will be built and executed by Claude in a Docker container on the connected node. Use this when you want the AI to handle the task autonomously instead of working on it locally.

name: spartanode_propose_gantt
description:
Analyze the current codebase and propose a Gantt chart (development roadmap).

**Two modes (auto-detected):**
1. **CREATE** — No Gantt exists yet. Scans the codebase (file tree, TODOs, README, dependencies, test gaps, git history) and produces a full task proposal.
2. **UPDATE** — Gantt already exists. Compares codebase state against existing tasks. Identifies new work needed, stale tasks, and gaps. Produces a diff proposal showing what to add/update/remove.

The output includes:
- Codebase analysis summary (languages, frameworks, structure, TODOs found)
- Current Gantt state (if UPDATE mode)
- Proposed tasks as a ready-to-use JSON array for `spartanode_sync_gantt`
- A human-readable summary of proposed changes

After reviewing the proposal, call `spartanode_sync_gantt` with the proposed tasks to apply them.

name: spartanode_screenshot_preview
description: Take a screenshot of the live preview pane in your workspace browser. Returns the rendered page as an image. Use this after making visual/UI changes to verify they look correct.

name: spartanode_select_port
description: Switch the live preview pane to show a different dev server port. Use this after starting a dev server to see it in the preview.

name: spartanode_resize_split
description: Resize the editor/preview split pane in the workspace. Ratio is the editor width as a fraction (0.2 = mostly preview, 0.8 = mostly editor).

name: spartanode_web_scrape
description:
Fetch a URL and extract clean, readable text content. Runs in the desktop app's main process (no CORS issues, no browser needed).

Best for: documentation sites, API references, static pages, markdown files, JSON endpoints, RSS feeds — anything where the content is in the HTML source.

Returns: extracted text (markdown-formatted with headings, links, code blocks, tables), page title, description. Optionally includes raw HTML and structured link/heading arrays.

For JavaScript-heavy SPAs where content is rendered client-side, use spartanode_browser_open + spartanode_browser_action instead.

name: spartanode_browser_open
description:
Open a persistent browser session on a URL. The session runs in a hidden Chromium webview with full JavaScript execution — it's a real browser.

Use this for:
- Testing the app you're building (open localhost:3000, click through flows)
- Scraping JS-heavy SPAs where spartanode_web_scrape returns empty content
- Filling forms, testing login flows, verifying UI state
- Any multi-step browser interaction

After opening, use spartanode_browser_action to interact with the page. Sessions persist across actions until you close them. Max 4 concurrent sessions.

name: spartanode_browser_close
description: Close a browser session and free its resources.

name: spartanode_browser_action
description:
Execute an action in a browser session. The session must be opened first with spartanode_browser_open.

Available actions:

**Reading page content:**
- `text` — Get page text (or text of a specific element with `selector`)
- `source` — Get full HTML source
- `title` — Get page title
- `url` — Get current URL
- `screenshot` — Capture page as an image
- `getElements` — Query elements by CSS selector, returns tag, text, href, bounds, visibility
- `getAttribute` — Get a specific attribute from an element

**Interacting with the page:**
- `click` — Click an element by CSS selector
- `type` — Type text into an input field (appends; use `clear: true` to clear first)
- `setValue` — Set input value directly (works with React controlled inputs)
- `select` — Set dropdown/select value
- `check` — Toggle a checkbox (set `checked: true/false`)
- `hover` — Hover over an element
- `focus` — Focus an element
- `scroll` — Scroll to coordinates (`x`, `y`) or to an element (`selector`)

**Navigation:**
- `navigate` — Go to a new URL (waits for page load)
- `back` / `forward` / `reload` — Browser history navigation

**Waiting:**
- `waitFor` — Wait for a CSS selector to appear in the DOM (uses MutationObserver, `timeoutMs` default 10s)

**Advanced:**
- `evaluate` — Run arbitrary JavaScript in the page context (`js` parameter)
- `cookies` — Get document.cookie
- `setCookie` — Set a cookie (`name`, `value`, optional `domain`, `path`)

name: spartanode_browser_screenshot
description:
One-shot screenshot: opens a URL, waits for rendering, captures a screenshot, and closes the session. Convenient shortcut when you just need to see what a page looks like without multi-step interaction.

For interactive testing (click, type, verify), use spartanode_browser_open + spartanode_browser_action instead.

name: spartanode_browser_list
description: List all open browser sessions. Shows session IDs, URLs, and whether each session is ready for commands.

name: spartanode_fetch_url
description:
Fetch a URL and return readable text content using raw HTTP fetch (fast, no JavaScript rendering).

Best for: documentation, API endpoints, static pages, markdown files, RSS feeds. Returns clean text with markdown formatting.

For JavaScript-heavy SPAs, use spartanode_scrape_page instead.

name: spartanode_scrape_page
description:
Scrape a page with full JavaScript rendering. Creates a hidden browser, loads the page, waits for JS to finish, then extracts text. Optionally returns a screenshot.

Use for SPAs (React, Vue, etc.) or pages that load content dynamically. Slower than spartanode_fetch_url but gets the fully rendered content.

name: spartanode_read_active_page
description:
Read the content of the currently active preview tab. No URL needed — reads whatever page is currently displayed in the browser pane.

Returns the page text, title, URL, and optionally a screenshot and raw HTML.

name: spartanode_navigate
description: Navigate the active preview tab to a URL. Waits for the page to load by default.

name: spartanode_go_back
description: Navigate back in the active preview tab's history.

name: spartanode_go_forward
description: Navigate forward in the active preview tab's history.

name: spartanode_open_tab
description: Open a new browser tab in the right pane with a URL.

name: spartanode_close_tab
description: Close a browser tab in the right pane.

name: spartanode_list_tabs
description: List all open browser tabs in the right pane. Shows tab IDs, URLs, titles, and which is active.

name: spartanode_get_console_logs
description:
Get recent console output from the active preview tab. Captures console.log, console.warn, console.error, etc.

Use this to check for JavaScript errors, API call logs, React warnings, or any runtime output from the app you're developing.

name: spartanode_run_js
description:
Execute JavaScript in the active preview tab and return the result. The code runs in the page's context — same as typing in Chrome DevTools console.

Use for: DOM inspection, reading state, checking values, counting elements, reading localStorage/cookies, or any custom query.

name: spartanode_click_element
description: Click an element on the page by CSS selector. The element is scrolled into view before clicking. Optionally waits after clicking and takes a screenshot.

name: spartanode_fill_input
description: Type text into an input field. Uses the native input setter to trigger React/Vue change detection. Optionally clears the field first and submits the form.

name: spartanode_get_elements
description:
Query the page for interactive elements. Returns a structured list with CSS selectors you can use with click/fill tools.

Default selector finds all links, buttons, inputs, selects, textareas, and elements with role="button" or onclick.

name: spartanode_select_option
description: Select an option from a <select> dropdown by value or visible text.

name: spartanode_scroll
description: Scroll the page or a specific element.

name: spartanode_active_tab_info
description: Report what's currently visible in the active right-pane tab (native app, webview URL, or SpartaNode itself). Use this to know what kind of context the unified tools (screenshot/click_at/type) will operate on. Cheap — no screenshot taken.

name: spartanode_screenshot
description: Take a screenshot of the active right-pane tab. Works for both webview and native apps. Use for visual verification AFTER an action, or for canvas apps where spartanode_inspect_app returns no elements. For native apps, prefer spartanode_inspect_app first — it's faster and gives structured data. Don't screenshot just to find button names; inspect gives those directly.

name: spartanode_click_at
description: Click at pixel coordinates. Last resort for native apps — prefer spartanode_click_by_name (clicks by accessibility name, headless) or spartanode_shortcut (keyboard shortcuts like Ctrl+S). Only use click_at for canvas-rendered apps where inspect_app returns no elements and you must visually identify coordinates from a screenshot.

name: spartanode_type
description: Type text into the focused element of the active right-pane tab. For webview tabs, the active element receives the text via the input/change event chain (works with React/Vue). For native tabs, the text is sent as keystrokes to the focused control. Click/focus an input first if needed.

name: spartanode_shortcut
description: THE PRIMARY WAY to interact with native apps. Send keyboard shortcuts — much faster and more reliable than clicking buttons or navigating menus. Works in every app, every locale. Use for: save (Ctrl+S), undo (Ctrl+Z), copy/paste (Ctrl+C/V), bold (Ctrl+B), italic (Ctrl+I), find (Ctrl+F), close (Alt+F4), new (Ctrl+N), print (Ctrl+P), select all (Ctrl+A), confirm dialogs (Enter), cancel (Escape), navigate fields (Tab). IMPORTANT: For saving files, prefer Ctrl+S (save to existing path) over Ctrl+Shift+S (Save As dialog). If the file doesn't exist yet and you need to save to a specific path, use the Bash/Write tool to write the file directly — do NOT try to automate the Save As dialog, it's unreliable.

name: spartanode_inspect_app
description: List interactive UI elements in the active app. Use for DISCOVERY — learning what's on screen (button names, menu items, text fields). Do NOT use repeatedly in a loop to "check state" — that's slow (~1s per call). After discovering element names, interact via spartanode_shortcut (preferred for common operations) or spartanode_click_by_name. IMPORTANT: Do not try to automate native file dialogs (Save As, Open, Print) via inspect+click — they are unreliable. Use filesystem tools (Bash/Write) for file I/O instead.

name: spartanode_click_by_name
description: Click a UI element by its accessibility name. Works headlessly (no focus needed). Good for clicking specific buttons, menu items, checkboxes, tabs. But for COMMON operations (save, bold, undo, copy, close), prefer spartanode_shortcut — it's faster and works without knowing the localized button name. Use click_by_name when there's no keyboard shortcut for the action (e.g. clicking a specific toolbar button, selecting a list item, toggling a checkbox).

name: spartanode_type_into
description: Type text into a UI element by its accessibility name. Works headlessly — the app doesn't need to be focused or visible. Uses UIA ValuePattern.SetValue on Windows, AXValue on macOS, AT-SPI2 EditableText on Linux. For text editors, this directly sets the content without keystroke simulation. Use spartanode_inspect_app first to find the element name (e.g. "Text Editor", "Search box", "URL bar"). For webview tabs, falls back to filling the input via DOM.

name: spartanode_select_text
description: Select a specific text string within a text element in the active native app. Uses UIA TextPattern to find and highlight the text. Useful for applying formatting: first select the text, then click the formatting button (e.g. Bold, Italic) with spartanode_click_by_name. The element parameter is the accessibility name of the text area (use spartanode_inspect_app to find it).

name: spartanode_office_action
description:
Execute an action on the active Microsoft Office document via COM automation. Works headlessly — much faster and more reliable than UIA for Office-specific operations. The target app (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) must already be running with a document open.

WORD actions: get_info, get_text, set_text, insert_text (at cursor), bold_selection, italic_selection, find_and_replace ({find, replace}), save, save_as ({path})
EXCEL actions: get_info, get_cell ({cell: "A1"}), set_cell ({cell: "A1", value: "hello"}), set_range ({start: "A1", data: [["a","b"],["c","d"]]}), get_range ({range: "A1:C10"}), save, save_as ({path})
POWERPOINT actions: get_info, add_slide ({title?, layout?}), set_slide_text ({slide: 1, shape: 1, text: "hello"}), save, save_as ({path})

Use this instead of UIA inspect+click for any Office data manipulation. For formatting that doesn't have a COM action here, use spartanode_shortcut (Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, etc.).

name: spartanode_open_document
description: Open a local document in a viewer tab in the right pane. Supports PDF, images (png/jpg/gif/svg/webp), Markdown, text, JSON, YAML, CSV, Word (.docx), and Excel (.xlsx).

name: spartanode_read_document
description: Extract text content from a local document file. Returns plain text for text-based files, extracted text for Word, structured JSON for Excel. For PDFs and images, use spartanode_open_document + spartanode_screenshot instead.

name: spartanode_list_native_apps
description: List all embedded native desktop applications. Shows app IDs, names, and process info.

name: spartanode_open_app
description: Open an installed Windows desktop application by name (e.g. "powerpoint", "slack", "notepad", "vscode") and embed it as a right-pane tab. Resolves the name against an index of Start Menu shortcuts. If multiple apps match, picks the most specific (shortest name); other candidates are returned in case the user wanted a different one. Use spartanode_list_installed_apps if you want to see what's available before picking.

name: spartanode_list_installed_apps
description: List installed Windows desktop applications discovered via the Start Menu shortcut scan. Use this to find the exact name of an app before calling spartanode_open_app, or to see what's available.

name: spartanode_refresh_installed_apps
description: Force a re-scan of Start Menu shortcuts to refresh the installed-apps index. Run this if the user just installed a new app and spartanode_open_app says it can't find it.

name: tradingview_scan
description: Scan US stocks with custom filters (price > X, RSI < 30, etc.). Returns up to `limit` rows with the requested columns.

name: tradingview_compare_stocks
description: Returns price, change, market cap, P/E, EPS, revenue, dividend yield, RSI, and analyst recommendation rating (-1 sell to +1 buy) for 2-5 stocks. Revenue growth rate and analyst price targets are not available.

name: tradingview_quote
description: Get a 15-minute delayed quote for one or more stock tickers (e.g. 'AAPL' or 'NASDAQ:AAPL'). Returns price, change, volume, market cap, and pre-market/after-hours data when available. Data is delayed ~15 minutes during market hours — use finnhub_quote for real-time prices if available. If a ticker returns empty results, retry with the correct exchange prefix (e.g. 'NYSE:CDE', 'AMEX:XYZ').

name: tradingview_technicals
description: Get technical indicators (RSI, MACD, moving averages, pivot points, etc.) for one or more stock tickers. If a ticker returns empty results, retry with the correct exchange prefix (e.g. 'NYSE:CDE', 'AMEX:XYZ').

name: tradingview_top_gainers
description: Get today's top gaining stocks by percentage change on a given exchange. Defaults to major US exchanges (NYSE, NASDAQ, AMEX) with market cap > $100M. OTC penny stocks excluded by default.

name: tradingview_top_losers
description: Get today's top losing stocks by percentage change on a given exchange. Defaults to major US exchanges (NYSE, NASDAQ, AMEX) with market cap > $100M. OTC penny stocks excluded by default.

name: tradingview_top_volume
description: Get stocks with the highest trading volume today. Defaults to major US exchanges.

name: tradingview_market_indices
description: Get real-time values for major market indices: VIX (volatility), S&P 500, NASDAQ Composite, and Dow Jones. Essential for gauging broad market conditions, risk sentiment, and options pricing context.

name: tradingview_sector_performance
description: Get performance of S&P 500 sector ETFs (XLK, XLF, XLE, XLV, XLI, XLP, XLU, XLY, XLC, XLRE, XLB). Shows which sectors are leading or lagging today. Essential for sector rotation analysis.

name: tradingview_volume_breakout
description: Find stocks with unusual volume (current volume significantly above average). Defaults to major exchanges.

name: crypto_scan
description: Scan cryptocurrency pairs using TradingView filters. Returns price, volume, and technical indicators.

name: crypto_quote
description: Get real-time quotes for specific crypto pairs. Supports 'BTCUSDT' (defaults to BINANCE) or 'BINANCE:BTCUSDT'.

name: crypto_technicals
description: Get technical analysis for crypto pairs. Supports 'BTCUSDT' or 'BINANCE:BTCUSDT'.

name: crypto_top_gainers
description: Get top gaining cryptocurrency pairs by percentage change. Defaults to major exchanges and volume > $10k.

name: edgar_search
description: Search SEC EDGAR filings by keyword. Best for finding mentions of specific trends, technologies, or events across all companies. Returns metadata including accession numbers, form types, and direct sec.gov links.

name: edgar_company_filings
description: Retrieve the most recent official filings for a specific company. Use this to find a company's latest 10-K (annual), 10-Q (quarterly), or 8-K (current events) reports.

name: edgar_company_facts
description: Retrieve high-fidelity financial metrics (Revenue, Net Income, EPS, Assets, Liabilities) directly from SEC XBRL data. This is more reliable than extracting numbers from text filings.

name: edgar_insider_trades
description: Monitor legal stock trades made by company executives and directors (Forms 3, 4, 5). Returns detailed transaction data including insider names, titles, buy/sell type, share amounts, and prices.

name: edgar_institutional_holdings
description: Track 'big money' moves by searching Form 13F filings. Use to find what hedge funds and institutional managers (e.g. 'Berkshire Hathaway') are holding or what firms own a specific ticker.

name: edgar_ownership_filings
description: Monitor significant changes in company ownership (5%+ stakes). Use 13D and 13G filings to identify activist investors (e.g. Carl Icahn, Ryan Cohen) entering or exiting a stock.

name: coingecko_coin
description: Get detailed cryptocurrency info from CoinGecko. Use slug IDs (e.g. 'bitcoin', 'ethereum', 'solana'), NOT ticker symbols.

name: coingecko_trending
description: Get trending cryptocurrencies on CoinGecko (top 7 by search popularity in last 24h).

name: coingecko_global
description: Get global cryptocurrency market statistics: total market cap, 24h volume, BTC/ETH dominance.

name: options_expirations
description: Get all available option expiration dates for a stock ticker. Call this first to discover valid dates, then pass one to options_chain or options_max_pain.

name: options_chain
description: Get the full option chain (calls and puts) with calculated Greeks (Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega). Use options_expirations first to find valid dates. If expiration is omitted, uses nearest date. By default, returns strikes within ±20% of current price to save tokens. Use strike_min/strike_max for custom range, or all_strikes=true for everything.

name: options_unusual_activity
description: Find options contracts with unusually high volume relative to open interest (a common 'smart money' signal). Scans the nearest expiration and flags contracts where volume/OI exceeds a threshold.

name: options_max_pain
description: Calculate the max pain strike price — where cumulative option open interest expires worthless. This level often acts as a support/resistance zone near expiration.

name: options_implied_move
description: Calculate the expected move implied by options pricing (ATM straddle). Essential for earnings plays — shows how much the market expects the stock to move. Compare implied vs historical moves to assess if premium is cheap or expensive.

name: options_put_call_ratio
description: Get historical put/call ratio from CBOE (market-wide sentiment indicator). Ratio > 1.0 = more puts (bearish sentiment), < 0.7 = more calls (bullish/complacent). Types: 'total' (all options), 'equity' (stock options only), 'index' (index options only).

name: sentiment_fear_greed
description: Get the CNN Fear & Greed Index for the US stock market. Returns a composite score (0-100) with rating (extreme fear/fear/neutral/greed/extreme greed) and 7 sub-indicators: S&P 500 momentum, stock price strength (52w highs vs lows), stock price breadth (McClellan), put/call ratio, VIX, junk bond demand, safe haven demand. Also includes previous close, 1-week, 1-month, and 1-year scores for trend context. Use this to gauge overall market sentiment before analyzing individual stocks.

name: sentiment_crypto_fear_greed
description: Get the Crypto Fear & Greed Index from Alternative.me. Returns a score (0-100) with rating (extreme fear/fear/neutral/greed/extreme greed). Based on Bitcoin volatility, market volume, social media, surveys, dominance, and trends. Use this alongside coingecko tools for crypto market context.

name: frankfurter_latest
description: Get latest forex exchange rates from the European Central Bank. Returns daily reference rates for 31 major currencies. Updated once per business day at ~16:00 CET. These are reference rates, not real-time trading rates.

name: frankfurter_historical
description: Get ECB forex exchange rates for a specific past date. Daily reference rates, not real-time trading rates. If the date is a weekend or holiday, returns the previous business day's rates. Data available from 1999-01-04 (Euro inception).

name: frankfurter_timeseries
description: Get daily ECB forex rate history for a date range (max 90 days). Daily reference rates, not real-time. Use for currency trend analysis. Only business days included (weekends/holidays omitted). Requires symbols filter to control response size.

name: frankfurter_convert
description: Convert an amount between two currencies at the latest ECB daily reference rate. Updated once per business day — not suitable for intraday trading rates. Useful for cross-border stock valuation and currency exposure calculations.

name: frankfurter_currencies
description: List all 31 currencies supported by the Frankfurter API with their full names. Use to look up valid currency codes before calling other frankfurter tools.

name: sverklo_context
description: Umbrella context bundler. Give a task description and get a single curated bundle: codebase overview header, semantically relevant code, related symbols, and matching saved memories — in one round trip. Use this as the FIRST call when you start working on a new task and want to orient quickly. PASS `budget` for a PageRank-pruned repo map fit to a token budget — the ideal way to give an agent a complete mental model of an unfamiliar codebase in one call.

name: sverklo_search
description: Hybrid semantic + text search with PageRank ranking. WORKS WELL for: exploratory questions where you don't know the exact symbol ('how does auth work', 'find anything related to billing', 'where's the retry logic'), anti-pattern discovery ('swallowed exceptions', 'silent null returns'), and cross-file semantic matches. STRUGGLES WITH: framework registration and wiring questions ('how is X registered as a bean', 'where is this interceptor configured'). For those, grep the specific annotation (@Component, @Configuration, etc.) directly. Response includes a confidence signal and a fallback hint when the query shape is one we know semantic search handles poorly.

name: sverklo_overview
description: Get a structural map of the codebase. Shows the most important files and their key symbols ranked by dependency importance (PageRank). Use this FIRST when starting work on an unfamiliar codebase or directory.

name: sverklo_lookup
description: Look up a specific symbol (function, class, type, variable) by name. Returns its full definition, signature, and location.

name: sverklo_refs
description: Find all references to a symbol across the codebase. Shows where a function, class, or type is imported, called, or used. Matches on identifier word boundaries by default — `embed` does NOT match `embeddingStore`. Pass `exact: false` to opt into substring matching.

name: sverklo_deps
description: Show what a file imports/depends on and what depends on it. Helps understand the impact of changing a file.

name: sverklo_status
description: Project state + tool usage guide. Returns index health (files, chunks, languages), memory summary, and specific tool recommendations tailored to this codebase. Call this first when starting a new session to understand what sverklo knows about the project.

name: sverklo_remember
description: Save a persistent memory tied to git state. Auto-invalidates conflicting prior memories.

name: sverklo_recall
description: Search memories semantically. Finds past decisions, preferences, and patterns relevant to a query. Supports two specialized modes: `mode=core` returns only the always-on project invariants (fast, no query needed — use at session start); `mode=archival` searches the full archive with semantic ranking; `mode=all` (default) searches both. Use core for 'what are the project-wide rules I must not violate' and archival for 'what did we decide about X on this codebase'.

name: sverklo_forget
description: Permanently delete a memory after recall returned a stale or wrong entry. Prefer sverklo_remember (with the new content) over forget+remember when superseding a decision — supersession preserves the audit trail via valid_until_sha + superseded_by; forget loses it. Get IDs from sverklo_recall or sverklo_memories.

name: sverklo_memories
description: List all memories for the current project, or surface conflict candidates. Default mode shows memory health (staleness, confidence, access frequency). Pass `mode: "conflicts"` to surface pairs of active memories that share a pin and may contradict — the bi-temporal model preserves both, so this is a review prompt for the agent or human, not an auto-resolution.

name: sverklo_promote
description: Promote a memory to the core tier. Core memories are auto-injected into every session via sverklo://context resource — use for project invariants that should always be in the AI's context (style rules, framework conventions, 'never do X' rules).

name: sverklo_demote
description: Demote a memory from core to archive tier. Archive memories are only retrieved on demand via sverklo_recall — not automatically injected. Use for memories that no longer need to be in every session.

name: sverklo_impact
description: Refactor blast-radius: callers of a symbol with confidence scoring. Run before editing. Use cross_repo:true to see impact across linked projects in a workspace.

name: sverklo_audit
description: One-call codebase health report: god nodes (highest blast-radius symbols), hub files (highest PageRank), orphan symbols (likely dead code), and language/memory stats. Use as the seed for a code-quality pass — pair with sverklo_impact for blast-radius and sverklo_deps for fan-in/fan-out. Cheaper than running overview + impact + dependencies separately.

name: sverklo_wakeup
description: 500-token codebase summary suitable for pasting into a system prompt when the agent has no MCP access. Use this when integrating sverklo intelligence into Cursor, Codex, or a CI bot that can't run the MCP server. For MCP-connected agents, prefer sverklo_status and the richer per-tool surfaces — they return more and stay in budget.

name: sverklo_review_diff
description: Diff-aware context bundler for code review. Takes a git ref or range and returns: changed files, semantic delta (added/removed/modified symbols), dangling references for removed symbols, impact set for modified symbols, and similar-symbol detection for added ones. Replaces 10-20 grep+read calls with one structured response. Use this FIRST when reviewing an MR/PR — it surfaces blast radius and convention violations grep cannot see.

name: sverklo_diff_search
description: Semantic search scoped to files in a git diff (and optionally their dependency closure). Use this when reviewing an MR/PR and you need to find code related to a query — but only within the changed files, not the entire codebase. Cuts noise from global search and lets you ask questions like 'find all lock acquisitions in the changed files' or 'where do these new functions get called from existing code'.

name: sverklo_test_map
description: Map a git diff to its test coverage. Given a ref/range, lists which tests likely cover each changed source file (via name heuristics + import graph), flags changed source files with NO matching tests, and shows which test files were modified in the diff. Use this during MR/PR review to answer 'what tests should I run?' and 'is this change tested?' without grepping the whole repo. Coverage is heuristic — sverklo doesn't run code, so treat results as candidates, not ground truth.

name: sverklo_ast_grep
description: Find code by AST shape, not text — e.g. 'every console.log($X)', 'every catch (e) { return null }'. Requires ast-grep on PATH. Pick this over sverklo_search when you need exact structural matches (consistent transformations, lint-style queries) and over Grep when you need to ignore identifier names or whitespace. Falls back to a clear error if ast-grep is missing.

name: sverklo_clusters
description: Group files into modules by graph-community detection (label propagation over the import graph). Returns 3+ file clusters with their hub file. Use this on first contact with an unfamiliar repo — pair with sverklo_concepts (after running `sverklo concept-index`) for an LLM-named summary of each cluster. Skip if the codebase has fewer than ~20 source files; structure won't be informative.

name: sverklo_pin
description: Pin a memory to a specific file or symbol. Pinned memories surface automatically when recalling by that file path or symbol name, without needing semantic search.

name: sverklo_unpin
description: Remove a pin from a memory.

name: sverklo_investigate
description: Single-call research primitive: fans out to BM25, embeddings, symbol lookup, and reference-expansion in parallel; RRF-fuses the candidates; returns one ranked bundle with per-hit provenance (which retriever(s) found it). Cheaper than running sverklo_search + sverklo_refs + sverklo_lookup back-to-back. WORKS WELL for open-ended questions where you don't yet know whether the answer lives in code, callers, or documentation — the `found_by` tags tell you which signal agreed. Use sverklo_search instead when you already know you want pure text/semantic retrieval.

name: sverklo_search_iterative
description: Wider-pool, iterative-friendly variant of sverklo_search. Returns a ctx:// handle to the top-200 candidate pool plus refinement hints (co-occurring symbols, dominant directories, concept overlap). Use ctx_grep / ctx_slice to refine without firing another retrieval. Worth the extra latency (~50ms) on hard multi-hop questions; for single-shot lookups use sverklo_search.

name: sverklo_ask
description: Natural-language router over sverklo's existing primitives. Maps a question to (a) the closest concept (if the concept index exists), (b) an investigate fan-out, and (c) refs/impact on the top symbols surfaced. Returns a structured answer with evidence — no generated prose. Use when you want a single keystroke that exercises the whole stack; for fine-grained control prefer sverklo_search / sverklo_investigate / sverklo_refs.

name: sverklo_verify
